Line-averaged argon density is the chord-averaged number density of argon ions along a line of sight through the plasma. The local argon ion density is understood as the sum over argon ionization stages, so the line average represents the effective argon ion content sampled by the chord.

The line average is defined by normalizing the line-integrated density by the chord length through the plasma:

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathrm{chord}} n_{\mathrm{Ar}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $l$ is distance along the chord in meters, $L$ is the chord length through the plasma in meters, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}(l)$ is the local argon ion number density in $m^{-3}$. The integral has units of $m^{-2}$, and division by $L$ gives a line-averaged density in $m^{-3}$.

In practice this quantity is obtained by first converting calibrated diagnostic signals to an argon density line integral, using the appropriate atomic physics, instrument response, and plasma-parameter modeling for the measurement. Raw brightness, spectral intensity, or other chord-integrated signals are not themselves line-averaged density; they must be interpreted as or transformed into $\int n_{\mathrm{Ar}} dl$ before normalization by the effective chord length.

Typical values are about $10^{14}-10^{16}\ m^{-3}$ for trace argon concentrations, $10^{16}-10^{18}\ m^{-3}$ during deliberate argon seeding or impurity transport studies, and can approach $10^{19}\ m^{-3}$ transiently during strong gas injection or disruption-mitigation scenarios.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_deuterium_density
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Chord-average of the deuterium ion number density along a diagnostic line of sight, equal to the path integral of the local deuterium density divided by the chord length.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged deuterium ion number density gives the mean deuterium particle density along a diagnostic chord through the plasma, providing a chord-path-weighted scalar measure of absolute deuterium content distinct from the isotopic fraction described by [volume_averaged_deuterium_fraction](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_fraction).

The quantity is defined as:

$$
\bar{n}_D = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_D(\ell) \, d\ell
$$

where $n_D(\ell)$ is the local deuterium ion number density in m$^{-3}$ at chord position $\ell$ and $L$ is the total chord length in m.

It is typically inferred from interferometric phase-shift measurements combined with isotope-resolved spectroscopy sensitive to deuterium Balmer emission. It complements the volume-based [volume_averaged_deuterium_density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and analogous chord-averaged fuel densities such as [line_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density) for protium and [line_averaged_helium_4_density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density) for helium-4.

Typical values range from $5 \times 10^{18}$ to $5 \times 10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$ in tokamak deuterium plasmas, scaling with the line-averaged electron density and the deuterium fuel fraction of the isotopic mix.
NAMES.sign: Positive when deuterium ions are present in the plasma along the measurement chord.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_effective_charge
NAMES.short: Line-averaged effective ion charge Zeff of the plasma, obtained as the chord-path integral of the local effective charge divided by the chord length.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged effective charge characterizes the mean impurity content of the plasma as sampled along a diagnostic line of sight. The local [effective charge](name:effective_charge) $Z_\text{eff}$ is defined as $Z_\text{eff} = \sum_i n_i Z_i^2 / n_e$, where $n_i$ is the number density of ion species $i$, $Z_i$ is the integer charge number of species $i$, and $n_e$ is the electron number density; deviations above unity indicate the presence of impurity ions heavier than hydrogen.

The line average integrates the local effective charge along a chord of length $L$:

$$
\langle Z_\text{eff} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L Z_\text{eff}(l) \, dl
$$

where $l$ is the coordinate along the chord.

This quantity is inferred from visible or near-ultraviolet bremsstrahlung continuum emission along a chord, whose emissivity scales as $\varepsilon \propto n_e^2 Z_\text{eff} T_e^{-1/2}$, where $T_e$ is the electron temperature; combining this signal with a simultaneous line-integrated electron density measurement yields $\langle Z_\text{eff} \rangle_L$ without requiring assumed spatial profile shapes. In a pure deuterium plasma $Z_\text{eff} = 1$; with typical light impurity content in reactor-relevant tokamak operation values of 1.5–3 are common, while heavy impurity seeding scenarios can yield values of 4–6. This chord-averaged quantity complements [volume_averaged_effective_charge](name:volume_averaged_effective_charge), which weights by the full plasma volume, and differs from [effective_charge_at_limiter](name:effective_charge_at_limiter), which is a boundary-localized evaluation.
NAMES.sign: Positive for any plasma with nonzero electron density, since $Z_\text{eff}$ equals the ratio of the charge-weighted ion density second moment to $n_e$, both of which are positive-definite quantities.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_electron_temperature
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Electron temperature averaged along a diagnostic chord through the plasma, equal to the path integral of the local electron temperature divided by the chord length.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged electron temperature collapses the radial [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature) profile into a single chord-weighted scalar, providing a global measure of plasma electron thermal content that depends on the diagnostic viewing geometry.

The defining relation is:

$$
\langle T_e \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L T_e(s) \, ds
$$

where $T_e(s)$ is the local electron temperature at position $s$ along the chord and $L$ is the total chord length.

This quantity is obtained by numerically integrating temperature profile measurements from multi-channel diagnostics such as Thomson scattering or electron cyclotron emission along the chord and normalizing to the chord length. Unlike the [volume_averaged_electron_temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature), it is sensitive to the specific chord geometry rather than reflecting a global plasma volume moment; unlike the [flux_surface_averaged_electron_temperature](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_temperature), it does not follow flux-surface topology, making its value dependent on the viewing angle and line-of-sight position relative to the plasma cross-section.

Typical values for a core-viewing chord in H-mode tokamak plasmas range from 1-5 keV; edge-chord geometries yield values of 0.1-1 keV.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron population has finite thermal kinetic energy, consistent with temperature being a non-negative measure of the mean thermal energy per particle.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_hydrogen_density
NAMES.subject: hydrogen
NAMES.short: Line-of-sight average of the hydrogen ion number density over a specified chord through the plasma. It represents the path-length-normalized hydrogen ion content, not neutral hydrogen density and not electron density.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged hydrogen density is the path-length average of the local hydrogen ion number density along a chosen chord through the plasma. Hydrogen density here denotes the density of hydrogen ions, excluding neutral hydrogen atoms and excluding electrons.

For a chord $C$ of averaging length $L$, the line average is defined by

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{H} \rangle_C = \frac{1}{L}\int_C n_\mathrm{H}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_\mathrm{H}(l)$ is the local hydrogen ion number density at path-length coordinate $l$, and $L = \int_C dl$ is the chord length over which the average is taken.

This quantity is generally inferred from a combination of constraints rather than measured directly by interferometric phase shift alone. Interferometry primarily constrains line-integrated electron density; hydrogen ion density is separated from electron density using quasineutrality together with composition information from spectroscopy, charge-exchange measurements, impurity modeling, particle balance, or transport analysis. In a nearly pure singly ionized hydrogen plasma it can be close to the line-averaged electron density, while impurity dilution, multiple ion species, and neutral populations make the hydrogen ion density distinct.

Typical line-averaged hydrogen ion densities in magnetically confined plasmas range from $10^{18}$-$10^{20}\ \mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with lower values in weakly fueled or edge-dominated conditions and higher values in high-density core plasmas.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_iron_density
NAMES.subject: iron
NAMES.short: Chord-average of the iron impurity ion number density, equal to the path integral of the local iron density divided by the chord length, summed over all ionization states.
NAMES.long:
The line-averaged iron density $\bar{n}_\mathrm{Fe}$ is the path-length-weighted average of the local iron impurity ion number density along a diagnostic chord, covering all ionization states from singly ionized to fully stripped iron. It provides a spatially integrated measure of iron contamination that is directly accessible to line-integrated spectroscopic diagnostics without requiring tomographic inversion of a local profile.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
\bar{n}_\mathrm{Fe} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_\mathrm{Fe}(l) \, dl
$$

where $l$ is the coordinate along the line of sight and $L$ is the total chord length traversing the plasma. This chord average relates directly to the parent local quantity [iron_density](name:iron_density), which gives the volumetric concentration at each spatial point. In contrast, [volume_averaged_iron_density](name:volume_averaged_iron_density) weights contributions by plasma volume element rather than by chord path length.

Iron enters magnetically confined plasmas primarily through sputtering and erosion of plasma-facing components, and elevated concentrations lead to significant radiative power losses. The line-averaged value is inferred from passive spectroscopy of iron line emission in the visible or vacuum ultraviolet range combined with ionization equilibrium modeling, or from impurity charge exchange spectroscopy on selected iron charge states. Typical line-averaged values range from $10^{14}$ to $10^{17}$ m$^{-3}$ depending on iron source strength, impurity transport, and plasma conditions. The iron_fraction provides a related dimensionless indicator of iron contamination normalized to electron density, while [line_averaged_nitrogen_density](name:line_averaged_nitrogen_density) is a sibling quantity measured by the same chord-averaging technique for a lighter impurity species.
NAMES.sign: Positive when iron ions are present along the measurement chord.

NAMES.name: line_averaged_tritium_density
NAMES.subject: tritium
NAMES.short: Tritium ion number density averaged along a measurement chord, computed as the path integral of local tritium density divided by the chord length.
NAMES.long:
Line-averaged tritium density is the chord average of the local tritium ion number density through a plasma. It gives a path-weighted measure of the tritium fuel-species content along the chosen sight line, without resolving variation along that line.

For a chord parameterized by path length $\ell$, the line average is defined by:

$$
\langle n_T \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_T(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $n_T(\ell)$ is the local tritium ion number density in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $\ell$ is distance along the chord in meters, $L$ is the chord length in meters, and $\langle n_T \rangle_L$ is in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$.

In practice, this quantity may be obtained by combining line-integrated density information with independent constraints on isotope composition; the diagnostic combination depends on plasma conditions and available measurements. It is conceptually analogous to [line_averaged_electron_density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), but refers only to tritium ions rather than all electrons.

Typical values in deuterium-tritium plasmas are about $0.1-8 \times 10^{19}\ \mathrm{m}^{-3}$, depending on total fuel density, tritium fraction, chord geometry, and radial density variation. The value is non-negative and is zero for a chord containing no tritium ions. For related tritium-density measures, compare with [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density) and [tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis).

NAMES.name: accumulated_ammonia_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short: Accumulated ammonia count is the total NH3 injected into the plasma vessel since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each ammonia molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons, equal to the total number of electrons in neutral NH3.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated ammonia count is the time-integrated amount of ammonia gas injected into the plasma vessel after plasma breakdown, represented as an equivalent-electron count rather than as a molecule count or particle inventory. For neutral ammonia, each $\mathrm{NH_3}$ molecule contains 10 electrons: 7 from nitrogen and 1 from each of the 3 hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is related to the injected molecular amount by:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3}}(t) = 10 \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the ammonia molecular injection rate, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma breakdown time. The factor 10 is stoichiometric and does not imply that the molecule is fully ionized at the point of injection.

In practice, this quantity is computed from calibrated gas-injection valve commands, flow-meter signals, reservoir pressure drops, or gas-box models, with corrections for line conductance, temperature, and valve response where available. It is an injected-source measure and may differ from the number of ammonia-derived particles that enter the confined plasma because of wall retention, dissociation, pumping, and edge neutral transport.

Typical values depend strongly on device size and gas-injection purpose. Small diagnostic or impurity-seeding puffs may correspond to about $10^{18}$-$10^{20}$ equivalent electrons, while larger fueling or disruption-mitigation injections can reach $10^{21}$-$10^{23}$ equivalent electrons.

NAMES.name: accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia_deuterated
NAMES.short: Accumulated deuterated ammonia (ND3) introduced after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ND3 molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons: 7 from nitrogen and 1 from each of the three deuterium atoms.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated deuterated ammonia count is the cumulative amount of neutral ND3 gas injected after plasma breakdown, expressed as the number of electrons associated with those neutral molecules in complete ionization accounting. It tracks delivered deuterated-ammonia inventory, not net plasma electron density or electric charge, and is the deuterated-isotopologue counterpart of [accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count).

The conversion from molecular injection to equivalent-electron count is

$$
N_\mathrm{eq}(t) = 10 \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \Gamma_{\mathrm{ND}_3}(t')\, dt'
$$

where $N_\mathrm{eq}$ is a dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{ND}_3}$ is the neutral ND3 molecular injection rate in molecules per second. The factor 10 is the neutral-molecule electron inventory, $7+1+1+1$, from nitrogen plus three deuterium atoms.

In practice this quantity is computed by integrating a calibrated ND3 molecular flow rate, commonly inferred from gas-injection hardware such as mass-flow controllers, pulsed valves, plenum pressure and temperature evolution, and calibrated line conductance. The accumulation starts at breakdown, increases during ND3 delivery, and remains unchanged when no deuterated ammonia is injected.

Typical values are strongly device- and scenario-dependent. Small calibrated impurity puffs may correspond to $10^{18}-10^{21}$ equivalent electrons, routine radiative-seeding injections to $10^{21}-10^{23}$ equivalent electrons, and large cooling or mitigation injections to $10^{23}-10^{25}$ equivalent electrons or higher.

NAMES.name: accumulated_argon_count
NAMES.subject: argon
NAMES.short: Cumulative count of argon delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory. The count increases by 18 for each argon atom, using the atomic number of argon.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated argon count is the time-integrated amount of argon delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented as a dimensionless equivalent-electron inventory. It counts injected argon atoms with a weighting equal to the argon atomic number, so one argon atom contributes 18 count units. This is an injected inventory measure, not a measure of free electrons, plasma content, retained argon, or ionization state.

The accumulated count is defined by integrating the argon atom injection rate from breakdown time:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}(t) = 18 \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron argon count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate in atoms per second, $t$ is time in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time in seconds. Argon introduced before breakdown belongs to the prefill contribution represented by [argon_count](name:argon_count), not to this accumulated post-breakdown quantity.

In practice, the injection rate is obtained from calibrated gas-valve systems, reservoir pressure drops, conductance models, or mass-flow measurements, and then integrated from the breakdown reference time. Because this quantity represents delivered gas, it is not decremented by subsequent ionization, radiation, pumping, exhaust, wall retention, or redistribution within the vessel. It is analogous to [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) and [accumulated_xenon_count](name:accumulated_xenon_count), with the numerical weighting set by the atomic number of each species, and can contribute to a total injected-particle inventory such as [accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection).

Typical values are about $10^{19}$-$10^{22}$ count units for routine argon puffs or impurity seeding, corresponding to roughly $6 \times 10^{17}$-$6 \times 10^{20}$ argon atoms. Larger disruption-mitigation injections can reach about $10^{22}$-$10^{24}$ count units, depending on the valve system, reservoir pressure, and mitigation strategy.

NAMES.name: accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: carbon
NAMES.short: Cumulative carbon injected by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with six counts per carbon atom.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated carbon count due to gas injection is the running total of carbon introduced after plasma breakdown by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each injected carbon atom contributes 6 to the dimensionless count, corresponding to the atomic number of carbon, so the value is non-negative and increases only when carbon-bearing gas is injected.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count is related to the carbon atom source rate by

$$
N_{C,\mathrm{acc}}(t) = 6 \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \Gamma_{C,\mathrm{gas}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{C,\mathrm{acc}}$ is the accumulated dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ and $t'$ are times in seconds, and $\Gamma_{C,\mathrm{gas}}$ is the injected carbon atom rate in atoms per second. The corresponding physical number of injected carbon atoms is $N_{C,\mathrm{acc}}/6$.

In practice this quantity is computed by integrating calibrated gas-injection flow rates from breakdown onward, converting molecular flow to carbon atom flow using the gas stoichiometry, and applying the factor of 6. It is the time integral of [carbon_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:carbon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and excludes the pre-breakdown inventory represented by [carbon_initial_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).

Typical values are 0 for pulses without deliberate carbon-bearing gas injection and about $10^{18}$-$10^{22}$ for trace or impurity-gas injection cases, depending on injected gas species, calibrated valve throughput, and injection duration.

NAMES.name: accumulated_ethane_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short: Cumulative ethane (C2H6) gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each ethane molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated ethane count tracks the time-integrated amount of ethane (C2H6) gas injected into the plasma vessel since plasma breakdown, expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. Each ethane molecule consists of two carbon atoms (atomic number $Z_C = 6$) and six hydrogen atoms (atomic number $Z_H = 1$), contributing $2 \times 6 + 6 \times 1 = 18$ equivalent electrons per molecule, so the accumulated count $N_{\rm acc}$ and the total number of injected molecules $N_{\rm mol}$ are related by:

$$
N_{\rm acc} = 18 \, N_{\rm mol}
$$

where $N_{\rm mol}$ is the number of ethane molecules delivered since plasma breakdown.

The accumulated count is obtained by integrating the instantaneous ethane injection rate from the moment of plasma breakdown. It provides a direct measure of the combined carbon and hydrogen impurity load introduced via ethane injection over the discharge. This quantity complements [ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count), which covers only the prefill phase preceding breakdown. Related hydrocarbon injection counts include [accumulated_propane_count](name:accumulated_propane_count) (C3H8, 26 electrons per molecule) and [ethylene_count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count) (C2H4, 16 electrons per molecule).
NAMES.sign: Positive when ethane gas is injected into the plasma vessel.

NAMES.name: accumulated_ethylene_count
NAMES.subject: ethylene
NAMES.short: Cumulative ethylene (C2H4) gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count where each ethylene molecule contributes 16 equivalent electrons (2 carbon atoms at Z = 6 each, 4 hydrogen atoms at Z = 1 each).
NAMES.long:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon hydrocarbon molecule in which each molecule contributes 2 carbon atoms (atomic number $Z_C = 6$) and 4 hydrogen atoms ($Z_H = 1$), yielding 16 equivalent electrons per molecule.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count is defined by:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 16 \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}}{dt'} \, dt'
$$

where $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the time of plasma breakdown and $dN_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}/dt$ is the instantaneous ethylene injection rate in molecules per second.

The integral runs from plasma breakdown onward, excluding any prefill contribution. The quantity is inferred from calibrated gas-valve flow measurements and tracks the hydrocarbon-based electron inventory added to the plasma, relevant to impurity seeding and disruption mitigation experiments. Closely related hydrocarbon counts include [accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) (C2H6, 18 equivalent electrons per molecule) and [accumulated_propane_count](name:accumulated_propane_count) (C3H8, 26 equivalent electrons per molecule). For the species-summed inventory across all injected gasses, see [accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection).

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Time-integrated helium-3 inventory added by gas injection since plasma breakdown, represented as an equivalent-electron count. Each helium-3 atom contributes 2 equivalent electrons because its atomic number is Z = 2.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated helium-3 count due to gas injection is the total amount of helium-3 introduced after plasma breakdown by gas injection, expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron count. The equivalent-electron convention weights each neutral helium-3 atom by its atomic number, so one injected helium-3 atom contributes two counts.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count is defined from the injected helium-3 atomic source rate:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{^{3}\mathrm{He}}(t) = 2 \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \Gamma_{^{3}\mathrm{He}}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{^{3}\mathrm{He}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $\Gamma_{^{3}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-3 atom injection rate in atoms/s. The factor 2 is the helium atomic number and converts atoms to equivalent electrons.

In practice this quantity is computed from calibrated gas-injection measurements such as valve flow calibrations, pressure-volume-temperature accounting, or mass-flow controller signals, with isotope-specific calibration for helium-3 when available. It represents gas injected after breakdown and is distinct from any prefill inventory present before the plasma is formed.

Typical accumulated values are about $10^{18}-10^{21}$ equivalent electrons for trace or minority helium-3 puffs, and can reach $10^{22}-10^{23}$ equivalent electrons in large devices or long pulses with deliberate helium-3 fueling.

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_3
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of helium-3 atoms introduced by gas injection during the prefill phase, reported as an equivalent electron count. Each helium-3 atom contributes two equivalent electrons because its atomic number is 2.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated helium-3 prefill count due to gas injection is the total amount of helium-3 admitted by gas valves before plasma breakdown, reported as an electron-equivalent particle count. It is an accounting convention for particle inventory: each neutral helium-3 atom contributes two equivalent electrons, but the gas need not be ionized during the prefill phase.

The electron-equivalent prefill count is obtained by integrating the helium-3 atomic injection rate over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,prefill}}(^{3}\mathrm{He}) = 2 \int_{t_{\mathrm{start}}}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He}}(t)$ is the helium-3 atomic injection rate in atoms s$^{-1}$, $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ is the start time of helium-3 prefill, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the breakdown time or end of the prefill phase in seconds, and the factor 2 converts atoms to equivalent electrons. The resulting count is dimensionless.

In practice this quantity is inferred from calibrated gas-valve flow, reservoir depletion, pressure-rise measurements, or gas-balance analysis integrated over the prefill interval. It counts the amount introduced by injection, not the amount retained in the vessel after pumping, wall adsorption, or ionization. It is closely related to [helium_3_initial_count](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection), is the prefill contribution to [accumulated_helium_3_count](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection), and is the helium-3 counterpart of [accumulated_helium_4_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection).

Typical values are $10^{19}$-$10^{22}$ equivalent electrons for small to medium devices and can approach $10^{23}$ equivalent electrons in large-volume machines or high-minority-fraction helium-3 prefills. These counts correspond to half as many injected helium-3 atoms and are often chosen to set the initial minority concentration for ion-cyclotron-resonance-heating scenarios.

NAMES.name: accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Time-integrated count of helium-4 atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons, where each helium-4 atom contributes 2 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated helium-4 gas injection count is the time-integrated total of helium-4 delivered via gas injection over the full discharge, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Unlike the phase-restricted quantity [accumulated_helium_4_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection), this quantity accumulates contributions from all injection phases — prefill, flat-top fueling, and ramp-down — and represents the total helium-4 gas throughput for the entire pulse, making it the discharge-level integral of [helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection).

The cumulative count is defined as:

$$
N_\text{acc}(t) = \int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{He}_4}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He}_4}$ is the instantaneous equivalent-electron injection rate and $t_0$ marks plasma breakdown. Since helium-4 has atomic number $Z = 2$, each atom contributes 2 equivalent electrons; the atomic particle count is therefore this value divided by 2. This equivalent-electron convention is shared across the gas-injection count family, including [accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection) and [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count), enabling uniform cross-species fueling accounting.

The accumulated count is obtained by integrating calibrated gas-valve flow signals over time and is used for helium inventory management, fueling budget analysis, and helium-ash simulation studies.
NAMES.sign: Positive when helium-4 is injected into the plasma vessel, increasing the accumulated equivalent-electron count.

NAMES.name: accumulated_krypton_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated krypton count is the running total of krypton atoms introduced since plasma breakdown, converted to an electron-equivalent basis where each krypton atom contributes $Z_{\rm Kr} = 36$ electron equivalents when fully stripped of its bound electrons.

The quantity is obtained by integrating the instantaneous injection rate $\dot{N}_{\rm Kr}$ over time from the moment of plasma breakdown $t_0$:

$$
N_{\rm Kr,eq} = Z_{\rm Kr} \int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{N}_{\rm Kr}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $Z_{\rm Kr} = 36$ is the atomic number of krypton and $\dot{N}_{\rm Kr}$ is in atoms per second. This is distinct from the prefill-phase contribution captured by [krypton_prefill_count](name:krypton_prefill_count), which records only the gas load introduced before breakdown. Krypton serves as a heavy radiative seed impurity for power exhaust management and as a disruption mitigation agent; the cumulative injection inventory is therefore essential for interpreting bolometric radiated-power fractions and spectroscopic charge-state distributions throughout the discharge. Analogous running totals are defined for other injected species, including [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) and [accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when krypton has been cumulatively injected into the plasma since breakdown.

NAMES.name: accumulated_lithium_count
NAMES.subject: lithium
NAMES.short: Cumulative amount of lithium supplied by gas injection after plasma breakdown, reported as an equivalent-electron count. Each lithium atom contributes 3 equivalent electrons, so the value is three times the injected lithium atom count over the post-breakdown interval.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated lithium count is the cumulative lithium supplied by gas injection after plasma breakdown, converted to an equivalent-electron count using the lithium atomic number 3. It excludes lithium present before breakdown or introduced by other sources unless those sources are part of the gas-injection flow being integrated. The corresponding accumulated lithium atom count, comparable to [lithium_count](name:lithium_count) when that quantity represents an inventory or prefill amount, is one third of this value.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count at time $t$ is defined by integrating the lithium atom injection rate from breakdown to that time:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Li,eqe}}(t) = 3 \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \Gamma_{\mathrm{Li}}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Li,eqe}}$ is the accumulated lithium count expressed as equivalent electrons, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the neutral lithium atom flow rate delivered by gas injection in atoms/s, $t'$ is the integration time in seconds, $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and the factor 3 is the atomic number of lithium.

In practice this quantity is computed by time-integrating calibrated gas-injection throughput, valve-command, pressure-drop, or mass-flow measurements after conversion to a lithium atom flow rate. Corrections may account for valve response, conductance of the injection line, reservoir temperature, and uncertainty in the fraction of commanded material that enters the plasma chamber.

Typical values depend strongly on device size and seeding scenario. Small experiments may accumulate about $10^{17}-10^{19}$ lithium atoms, corresponding to $3 \times 10^{17}-3 \times 10^{19}$ equivalent electrons, while deliberate injection in medium or large tokamak discharges can reach about $10^{19}-10^{21}$ lithium atoms, corresponding to $3 \times 10^{19}-3 \times 10^{21}$ equivalent electrons.

NAMES.name: accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: methane_carbon_13
NAMES.short: Cumulative equivalent-electron count for carbon-13-labeled methane injected after plasma breakdown. Each 13CH4 molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons, using atomic number 6 for carbon and 1 for each of the four hydrogen atoms.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated carbon-13 methane count due to gas injection is the running equivalent-electron count associated with neutral ${}^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ molecules admitted after plasma breakdown. The carbon isotope label identifies the injected tracer species, while the electron-budget conversion is the same as for ordinary methane because ${}^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and ${}^{13}\mathrm{C}$ have the same nuclear charge. The accumulation starts from zero at plasma breakdown and remains constant during intervals with no ${}^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ injection.

The accumulation at time $t$ is defined from the molecular injection rate by:

$$
N_\mathrm{acc}(t) = 10 \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \dot{n}_{{}^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $N_\mathrm{acc}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time in seconds, $t$ and $t'$ are times in seconds, and $\dot{n}_{{}^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the calibrated molecular injection rate in molecules per second. The factor $10 = Z_\mathrm{C} + 4 Z_\mathrm{H}$ uses $Z_\mathrm{C}=6$ for carbon and $Z_\mathrm{H}=1$ for each hydrogen atom.

In practice this quantity is computed by integrating calibrated gas-valve or mass-flow measurements over the discharge, with corrections for valve conductance, reservoir pressure, gas temperature, and isotopic purity when needed. It is an isotope-resolved component of [accumulated_gas_count](name:accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection) and is directly comparable with accumulated_methane_count_due_to_gas_injection, [accumulated_deuterated_methane_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_deuterated_methane_count_due_to_gas_injection), [accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection), and [accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection) in particle and wall-retention accounting.

Typical accumulated values for small ${}^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ tracer puffs are $10^{17}$-$10^{20}$ equivalent electrons per discharge. Larger calibration, fueling, or wall-conditioning injections can reach $10^{20}$-$10^{22}$ equivalent electrons; the corresponding number of injected ${}^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ molecules is one tenth of the equivalent-electron count.

NAMES.name: accumulated_neon_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of neon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated neon count is the running temporal integral of the neon gas injection rate from plasma breakdown onward, giving the total neon inventory delivered to the plasma vessel over the discharge. Each injected neon atom contributes to the tally in equivalent-electron units — the raw particle count scaled by the neon atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Ne} = 10$ — enabling direct comparison with other injected fuel and impurity species.

The defining integral is:

$$
N_\mathrm{acc}(t) = Z_\mathrm{Ne} \int_{t_0}^{t} \dot{n}_\mathrm{Ne}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $\dot{n}_\mathrm{Ne}$ is the instantaneous neon injection rate in atoms per second, $t_0$ is the time of plasma breakdown, and $Z_\mathrm{Ne} = 10$ is the neon atomic number.

This quantity is determined from calibrated gas valve flow measurements integrated temporally throughout the discharge. It is particularly relevant in impurity seeding and disruption mitigation experiments where the cumulative neon dose governs radiated power fractions and pedestal stability.

The parent [neon_count](name:neon_count) provides phase-specific or instantaneous counts; [neon_prefill_count](name:neon_prefill_count) covers the pre-breakdown injection phase exclusively. Analogous accumulated quantities for other injected species include [accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection) and [accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection).
NAMES.sign: Positive when neon gas is injected, so the accumulated count increases monotonically from zero at plasma breakdown.

NAMES.name: accumulated_propane_count
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short: Accumulated propane count is the time-integrated amount of injected propane after plasma breakdown, converted to the number of electrons contained in the corresponding neutral propane molecules. One propane molecule contributes 26 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated propane count is the cumulative amount of propane gas injected after plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It is an atomic-accounting quantity: a neutral propane molecule, $\mathrm{C_3H_8}$, contains 26 electrons, so the value is 26 times the number of injected propane molecules rather than a direct measurement of plasma electrons.

The count at time $t$ can be defined from the molecular injection rate:

$$
N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,eq}}(t) = 26 \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \Phi_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,eq}}$ is dimensionless, $\Phi_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the propane molecular flow rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, $t$, $t'$, and the breakdown time $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are in seconds, and $26 = 3\times6 + 8\times1$ is the number of bound electrons in one neutral propane molecule.

In practice, the value is computed by integrating a calibrated propane flow over the interval beginning at plasma breakdown. If the available flow is molar, in mol s$^{-1}$, it is first multiplied by Avogadro's constant to obtain molecules s$^{-1}$; if it is given as a gas throughput or volume flow, it is converted to molecule rate using the relevant gas calibration before applying the electron-count conversion. The quantity complements [propane_prefill_count](name:propane_prefill_count) for pre-breakdown inventory and is analogous to [accumulated_ethane_count](name:accumulated_ethane_count) for another hydrocarbon species.

Typical values are 0 when no propane is injected, about $10^{18}$-$10^{21}$ for small trace or impurity-seeding puffs, and up to $10^{22}$-$10^{23}$ for larger or longer injections. These values represent injected inventory; they do not by themselves specify the retained amount, ionization fraction, or resulting plasma electron density.

NAMES.name: accumulated_silane_count
NAMES.subject: silane
NAMES.short: Accumulated silane gas injection since plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated silane count is the time-integrated amount of silane, SiH4, injected into the plasma after breakdown. The count is dimensionless and uses an equivalent-electron convention: one SiH4 molecule corresponds to 18 equivalent electrons, from silicon with atomic number 14 and four hydrogen atoms with atomic number 1.

The accumulated count at time $t$ is defined from the silane source rate by

$$
N_{\mathrm{SiH_4,acc}}(t) = \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4,eq}}(t')\,dt' = 18\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4,mol}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{SiH_4,acc}}$ is the accumulated dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time in seconds, $t'$ is time in seconds, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate in s^-1, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{SiH_4,mol}}$ is the molecular silane injection rate in molecules per second. The factor 18 is a counting convention for the injected molecular species, not a statement that neutral SiH4 supplies free electrons before dissociation or ionization.

In practice this quantity is computed by integrating the calibrated [silane source rate](name:silane_source_rate) from plasma breakdown onward. Gas present as vessel prefill or static inventory before breakdown is excluded; only deliberately injected silane during the plasma discharge contributes.

Typical values are 0 for discharges without silane injection. When silane is deliberately puffed for wall conditioning or impurity seeding, accumulated values are often about 10^18-10^22 in the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, depending on pulse duration, valve calibration, and injection recipe.

NAMES.name: accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: particle
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of particles delivered by gas injection since plasma breakdown, summed over all injected species and converted to an equivalent-electron count. The count resets at each new plasma breakdown event and is non-decreasing within a discharge while injection continues.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated total particle count due to gas injection is the time-integrated amount of neutral gas delivered after plasma breakdown, summed over all injection systems and injected species. Each species is weighted by the number of electrons carried by one neutral injected particle when fully ionized, so the result is a dimensionless equivalent-electron count rather than a molecule count alone. The accumulator is reset to zero at each new plasma breakdown event.

The accumulated count can be written as the species-weighted time integral of the injection rates:

$$
N_{\mathrm{tot}}(t) = \sum_s Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \Gamma_s(t') \, dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $\Gamma_s$ is the neutral-particle injection rate of species $s$ in $s^{-1}$, and $Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the number of bound electrons in one neutral injected particle of species $s$ when fully ionized. With non-negative injection rates the value is monotonic between resets and remains constant between gas pulses.

In practice, this quantity is computed by integrating calibrated gas-valve throughput, flow-meter measurements, or reconstructed injected particle rates over time, then applying the species weights before summing. It uses the same equivalent-electron normalization as [accumulated_total_gas_count](name:accumulated_total_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection), while specifically identifying the contribution from gas injection. If injector groups are reported separately, [accumulated_total_lower_gas_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_gas_particle_count_at_inlet_due_to_gas_injection) and accumulated_total_upper_gas_particle_count_due_to_gas_injection are partial sums whose total equals the vessel-wide value when the partition covers all gas injectors.

Typical accumulated values are $10^{20}$-$10^{23}$ equivalent electrons for small or short-pulse experiments and $10^{22}$-$10^{25}$ equivalent electrons for larger tokamak discharges, depending on fueling rate, pulse duration, gas species, and whether large pre-programmed gas puffs are included. Short diagnostic or impurity puffs can contribute smaller increments, often $10^{18}$-$10^{21}$ equivalent electrons.

NAMES.name: accumulated_xenon_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of xenon atoms from gas injection accumulated since plasma breakdown, expressed in equivalent electrons, where each xenon atom contributes 54 equivalent electrons corresponding to its atomic number Z = 54.
NAMES.long:
The accumulated xenon count tracks the total xenon atoms introduced by gas injection from plasma breakdown onward, expressed as a dimensionless equivalent-electron tally in which each neutral xenon atom contributes 54 counts equal to its atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} = 54$.

The defining integral is:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t) = 54 \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dt'} \, dt'
$$

where $dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}/dt'$ is the instantaneous xenon injection rate in atoms s$^{-1}$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the time of plasma breakdown in s, and $N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}$ is dimensionless. The prefill xenon inventory prior to breakdown is excluded from this integral and is tracked separately by [accumulated_xenon_prefill_count](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count).

The instantaneous injection rate contributing to this integral is characterized by [xenon_source_rate](name:xenon_source_rate). Xenon is employed as a high-$Z$ impurity in disruption mitigation and radiative cooling experiments; in massive gas injection scenarios the equivalent-electron count can reach $10^{23}$–$10^{24}$. For lighter noble gas comparisons, see [accumulated_neon_count](name:accumulated_neon_count) ($Z = 10$) and [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) ($Z = 36$).
NAMES.sign: Positive when xenon gas is injected into the vessel after plasma breakdown, incrementing the cumulative count.

NAMES.name: accumulated_xenon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: xenon
NAMES.short: Accumulated xenon prefill count is the end-of-prefill neutral xenon inventory expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each xenon atom contributes 54 to the dimensionless count.
NAMES.long:
Accumulated xenon prefill count is the scalar final value of the xenon gas dose introduced during the plasma prefill interval, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rather than as a count of neutral atoms. The conversion uses the xenon atomic number, so each neutral xenon atom contributes 54 equivalent electrons to the dimensionless count with unit 1.

The end-of-prefill count is defined from the integrated neutral xenon atom flow over the prefill time window:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Xe,prefill}}^{\mathrm{eq}}(t_{\mathrm{end}}) = 54\,N_{\mathrm{Xe,prefill}}(t_{\mathrm{end}}) = 54 \int_{t_{\mathrm{start}}}^{t_{\mathrm{end}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Xe,prefill}}^{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Xe,prefill}}$ is the accumulated number of xenon atoms, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the neutral xenon atom flow rate in atoms per second, $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ is the start of prefill injection, and $t_{\mathrm{end}}$ is the end of the prefill interval, usually before plasma breakdown.

In practice the value is computed by integrating a calibrated xenon gas-flow or inventory estimate over the prefill interval. It is an accumulated final-time dose, not an instantaneous flow rate, and is the xenon-specific prefill analog of [accumulated_xenon_count](name:accumulated_xenon_count) when restricted to the prefill phase.

Typical values are highly device- and scenario-dependent because prefill dosing depends on vessel volume, pumping, gas-valve calibration, and the intended initial neutral composition; the standard name therefore specifies the counting convention rather than a universal numerical range.

NAMES.name: ammonia_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ammonia
NAMES.short: Accumulated ammonia gas injected during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count.
NAMES.long:
Ammonia prefill count is the accumulated amount of NH$_3$ introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as the number of bound electrons carried by the injected neutral molecules. The convention uses the full stoichiometric electron content of ammonia, not the instantaneous ionization state of the gas.

For a number of injected ammonia molecules $N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$, the equivalent-electron count is

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}} = 10\,N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}
$$

where the factor 10 is the total electron count of one neutral NH$_3$ molecule: 7 from nitrogen and 3 from hydrogen.

In practice this quantity is computed from the time-integrated ammonia gas throughput during the prefill interval, using calibrated valve, pressure, flow, or reservoir-depletion measurements to infer the number of NH$_3$ molecules delivered. It is specific to the prefill phase and is conceptually distinct from an accumulated ammonia count over a longer or differently defined injection interval.

Typical values are strongly device and scenario dependent. Small conditioning or trace-species prefills may be around $10^{19}$-$10^{21}$ equivalent electrons, while larger dedicated molecular-gas prefills can reach $10^{22}$-$10^{23}$ equivalent electrons or more.

NAMES.name: atomic_count_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Total number of individual atoms in a pellet, with each atom counted once regardless of whether the propellant material is monatomic, diatomic, or molecular in form.
NAMES.long:
The atomic count of a pellet is the total discrete number of atoms present throughout the entire pellet body, tallied individually without regard to the molecular or bonding state of the constituent propellant material. A diatomic fuel such as D$_2$ (frozen deuterium) contributes two atoms per molecule; monatomic species contribute one atom per particle. This whole-pellet total differs from spatially resolved counterparts such as [outer_atomic_count_of_pellet](name:outer_atomic_count_of_pellet), and extends the general atom-counting convention of [count_of_pellet](name:count_of_pellet).

The atomic count $N_\mathrm{at}$ relates to the number of propellant molecules $N_\mathrm{mol}$ by:

$$
N_\mathrm{at} = \nu \, N_\mathrm{mol}
$$

where $\nu$ is the number of atoms per molecule of the propellant species (for example, $\nu = 2$ for D$_2$ or DT, and $\nu = 1$ for a monatomic noble gas).

The count is determined from the pellet geometry combined with the atomic number density of the solid propellant at cryogenic storage temperature, or from pellet mass measured immediately before injection. Fueling and disruption-mitigation pellets for large tokamaks contain on the order of $10^{21}$–$10^{23}$ atoms. The [normalized_atomic_count_of_pellet](name:normalized_atomic_count_of_pellet) expresses this total scaled against a reference count for nondimensional comparison across pellet types or injection scenarios.

NAMES.name: core_density_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Number density of a constituent atomic species in the inner core layer of a pellet used by a shattered-pellet injector.
NAMES.long:
Core density of pellet is the number density of a specified atomic species within the pellet's inner core layer. It represents how many atoms of that species are present per unit volume of the core material and is non-negative by physical definition.

The density is defined by the species population in the core divided by the core volume:

$$
n_{s,\mathrm{core}} = \frac{N_{s,\mathrm{core}}}{V_\mathrm{core}}
$$

where $n_{s,\mathrm{core}}$ is the core species number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{s,\mathrm{core}}$ is the number of atoms of species $s$ in the core and is dimensionless, and $V_\mathrm{core}$ is the core volume in m$^3$.

In practice this quantity is obtained from the specified pellet composition and core geometry, or equivalently from the total core species inventory normalized by the core volume. It is species-resolved: different atomic constituents of the same core can have different values.

No device-independent typical numerical range is implied by the standard name alone; values depend on the chosen pellet material, mixture, and core volume.

NAMES.name: deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Cumulative number of deuterium atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as equivalent electrons. Each deuterium atom contributes one count; deuterium introduced during the prefill phase is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium count due to gas injection is the accumulated amount of deuterium delivered by gas puffing or valve injection after plasma breakdown. It is expressed as an equivalent-electron particle count: because deuterium has atomic number one, each injected neutral deuterium atom contributes one count. Deuterium supplied before breakdown belongs to [deuterium_prefill_count](name:deuterium_prefill_count) rather than this quantity.

The accumulated count is the time integral of the deuterium injection source rate from the breakdown time to the time of interest:

$$
N_D^\mathrm{inj}(t) = \int_{t_\mathrm{bd}}^{t} \dot{N}_D^\mathrm{inj}(t') \, dt'
$$

where $N_D^\mathrm{inj}$ is the accumulated deuterium equivalent-electron count with unit $1$, $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma breakdown time in s, $t$ and $t'$ are times in s, and $\dot{N}_D^\mathrm{inj}$ is the [deuterium source rate due to injection](name:deuterium_source_rate_due_to_injection) in atoms/s, equivalently counts/s for deuterium.

In practice, the count is computed by integrating calibrated deuterium gas flow rates from injection valves, gas lines, or plenum pressure changes, with corrections for gas temperature, isotopic purity, valve calibration, and molecular composition when relevant. Contributions from all deuterium injection paths are summed, while prefill inventory and non-gas fueling sources are kept separate.

Typical accumulated values are dimensionless counts of about $10^{20}$-$10^{23}$ for short or medium tokamak pulses, and can reach $10^{24}$-$10^{25}$ in large-device or long-pulse operation depending on fueling demand, plasma density, and discharge duration.

NAMES.name: deuterium_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: deuterium
NAMES.short: Accumulated deuterium introduced by gas injection during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Because deuterium has atomic charge Z = 1, each deuterium atom contributes one count; deuterium from wall recycling, neutral beams, pellets, or later fueling is excluded.
NAMES.long:
Deuterium prefill count is the accumulated amount of deuterium introduced as neutral gas before plasma breakdown, expressed as the number of electrons that would be supplied by complete ionization. For deuterium, the atomic charge is $Z_D = 1$, so the equivalent-electron count is numerically equal to the number of injected deuterium atoms. The quantity is limited to the prefill gas-injection phase and excludes deuterium supplied later by fueling, wall recycling, pellets, or neutral beam injection.

The accumulated count is obtained by integrating the injected atomic deuterium rate over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{D,\mathrm{prefill}} = \int_{t_\mathrm{start}}^{t_\mathrm{end}} Z_D\,\dot{N}_D(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{D,\mathrm{prefill}}$ is the deuterium prefill count, $Z_D = 1$ is the deuterium atomic charge, $\dot{N}_D(t)$ is the atomic deuterium injection rate in atoms s$^{-1}$, and $t_\mathrm{start}$ and $t_\mathrm{end}$ are the start and end times of the prefill interval in s. If the measured gas throughput is a molecular $D_2$ rate, the corresponding atomic rate is twice the molecular rate.

In practice this quantity is computed from calibrated gas-valve commands, mass-flow measurements, pressure-drop calibrations, or reservoir inventory changes, with corrections for line volume, gas temperature, valve conductance, and species purity when needed. It represents the requested or delivered neutral-gas inventory before breakdown, not the amount that remains confined after ionization.

Typical prefill inventories are about $10^{20}-10^{23}$ equivalent-electron counts in small and medium tokamaks, and may approach $10^{24}$ in large devices or high-pressure prefill scenarios.

NAMES.name: electron_source_rate_due_to_injection
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Instantaneous electron-equivalent source rate supplied by plasma injection systems. It is the sum over injected atomic species of nuclear charge number times the atomic injection rate, representing the electron inventory that the injected material can contribute after ionization.
NAMES.long:
Electron source rate due to injection is the electron-equivalent particle rate delivered to the plasma or vessel by fueling or material injection systems. It counts the number of electrons per second associated with the injected atoms after ionization, and is used for particle inventory and density-control accounting rather than as a local ionization-rate density.

For a mixture of injected atomic species, the rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{inj}} = \sum_s Z_s\,\dot{N}_{s,\mathrm{inj}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{inj}}$ is the electron-equivalent injection rate, $s$ indexes the injected atomic species, $Z_s$ is the nuclear charge number of species $s$, and $\dot{N}_{s,\mathrm{inj}}$ is its atomic injection rate. Molecular flows are converted to atomic rates before applying the sum; for example, each injected $\mathrm{D}_2$ molecule contributes two deuterium atoms and therefore two electron equivalents after complete ionization.

In practice this quantity is computed from calibrated gas-valve throughput, pellet or compact-toroid particle content, or other injector flow measurements combined with the specified species composition. It may represent a single injector, a subsystem, or the total injected electron-equivalent rate, depending on the physical scope being described.

Typical values span about $10^{19}$-$10^{23}$ s$^{-1}$ for ordinary gas fueling valves in present-day tokamaks. Short high-throughput events such as massive gas injection or pellet injection can reach about $10^{22}$-$10^{25}$ s$^{-1}$ for brief intervals.

NAMES.name: ethane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: ethane
NAMES.short: Accumulated ethane gas injected during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each C2H6 molecule contributes 18 equivalent electrons.
NAMES.long:
Ethane prefill count is the accumulated amount of ethane introduced before plasma initiation, expressed as the number of electrons that would be supplied if the injected molecules were fully ionized. The quantity represents the ethane contribution to the initial neutral inventory in an equivalent-electron convention.

The conversion from injected ethane molecules to equivalent-electron count is:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}} = 18\,N_{\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6}
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}$ is the ethane prefill count, a dimensionless count of equivalent electrons, and $N_{\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6}$ is the accumulated number of injected ethane molecules, a dimensionless molecule count. The factor 18 is the total nuclear charge of one ethane molecule: two carbon atoms with charge 6 each plus six hydrogen atoms with charge 1 each.

In practice, the value is obtained from calibrated gas-delivery accounting over the defined prefill interval and converted from delivered molecular amount to equivalent-electron count. It should include ethane delivered for the prefill phase only, not later gas injection used for fueling, impurity control, or other discharge phases.

Typical values are strongly device- and scenario-dependent. They may be zero when ethane is not used for prefill, while intentional nonzero prefill amounts can span roughly $10^{19}$-$10^{23}$ equivalent electrons in small to medium devices and scale upward with vessel volume, target fill pressure, and delivered gas inventory.

NAMES.name: gas_flow
NAMES.short: Volumetric throughput rate of gas in an injection or pumping system, expressed as the product of local gas pressure and volumetric flow speed.
NAMES.long:
The gas flow $Q$ characterizes the pressure-weighted volumetric throughput of gas in a plasma-facing gas handling system, encompassing injection valves, injection pipes, and pumping ducts. It is the primary quantity governing particle delivery to and removal from the plasma vessel, directly linking hardware actuator settings to the plasma particle inventory.

The defining relation is:

$$
Q = p \cdot \dot{V}
$$

where $p$ is the local gas pressure and $\dot{V}$ is the volumetric flow rate. This standard vacuum-engineering throughput convention yields a quantity proportional to particle flux that remains well-defined independent of downstream pressure variations, making it the natural actuator variable for density control systems.

In gas injection applications, $Q$ acts as the primary actuator for plasma fueling, impurity seeding, and density control. In pumping ducts, it quantifies the particle exhaust rate entering the plasma particle balance as a sink. The operational dynamic range of a given valve or duct is bounded by [maximum_gas_flow](name:maximum_gas_flow) as the upper limit and [minimum_gas_flow](name:minimum_gas_flow) as the lower limit. The species-resolved pumping counterpart is neutral_species_flow.

Flow rates are inferred from calibrated mass flow controllers, pressure transducers combined with valve conductance models, or response-curve look-up tables that map control voltage to throughput. Typical injection rates range from $10^{-3}$ to $10$ Pa·m³·s⁻¹ for trace impurity valves through high-throughput fueling manifolds; pumping duct rates in large-scale devices can exceed $10$ Pa·m³·s⁻¹ during high-density operation.

NAMES.name: helium_4_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
NAMES.subject: helium_4
NAMES.short: Total neutral helium-4 gas injected during the prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with two electrons per helium-4 atom.
NAMES.long:
Helium-4 prefill count due to gas injection is the total equivalent-electron inventory supplied by externally injected neutral helium-4 during the prefill phase. Each helium-4 atom contributes two electron equivalents for complete ionization, so this is a gas-inventory bookkeeping count rather than a count of free electrons before breakdown.

The total over the selected prefill interval is obtained by integrating the neutral helium-4 atom injection rate and multiplying by the helium electron yield:

$$
N_{\mathrm{e,eq}}^{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}} = 2 \int_{t_\mathrm{start}}^{t_\mathrm{end}} \Gamma_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $\Gamma_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the neutral helium-4 atom injection rate in atoms s$^{-1}$, $t_\mathrm{start}$ is the start of helium-4 prefill gas admission, and $t_\mathrm{end}$ is the evaluation endpoint of the prefill interval, commonly just before plasma breakdown. The related [accumulated_helium_4_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection) is the same integral retained as a function of its upper time limit; evaluating it at $t_\mathrm{end}$ gives this total.

In practice, the count is inferred from calibrated helium-4 gas throughput, isotopic mixture fraction, valve-flow calibration, or an equivalent gas balance over the prefill interval. Only the injected helium-4 component is included; helium-3, other gas species, wall-released or recycled neutrals, and postbreakdown fueling are excluded. A helium-4 atom count, as opposed to this equivalent-electron count, is smaller by a factor of 2.

Typical values range from $10^{18}$-$10^{22}$ equivalent electrons in small and medium devices and from $10^{22}$-$10^{24}$ equivalent electrons in large tokamak prefill scenarios, depending on vessel volume, target neutral pressure, gas temperature, and prefill duration.

NAMES.name: krypton_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: krypton
NAMES.short: Equivalent electrons from krypton injected during the prefill phase; it is 36 times the number of krypton atoms delivered and is not the raw atom count.
NAMES.long:
Krypton prefill count is a bookkeeping measure of the neutral krypton inventory introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It converts the number of krypton atoms delivered during the prefill phase into the number of electrons those atoms would contain if fully counted by atomic number, enabling comparison with other species inventories.

The equivalent-electron count is defined from the injected krypton atom count as:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,e}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}} = 36 N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is the number of krypton atoms injected during the prefill phase and $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the atomic number of krypton. Both $N_{\mathrm{eq,e}}^{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ are dimensionless counts.

In practice, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}$ is obtained by integrating a calibrated krypton flow over the prefill time interval. For particle flow $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ in atoms s$^{-1}$, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}=\int \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt$; for molar flow $\dot{n}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ in mol s$^{-1}$, $N_{\mathrm{Kr,prefill}}=N_A\int \dot{n}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t)\,dt$; and for gas throughput $Q$ in Pa m$^3$ s$^{-1}$ at gas temperature $T$ in K, the ideal-gas estimate is $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}\approx Q/(k_B T)$, where $N_A$ is Avogadro's constant and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant. The same equivalent-electron inventory convention is used for related prefill or gas-injection quantities such as [argon_prefill_count](name:argon_prefill_count), [neon_prefill_count](name:neon_prefill_count), [tritium_prefill_count](name:tritium_prefill_count), [accumulated_xenon_prefill_count](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count), [accumulated_helium_4_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_helium_4_count_due_to_gas_injection), and [carbon_initial_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection); [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) denotes the krypton inventory accumulated beyond the prefill-only interval.

Typical values are strongly device- and recipe-dependent. Trace or calibration prefills may be about $10^{18}$-$10^{20}$ equivalent electrons, while larger high-atomic-number gas puffs can reach $10^{21}$-$10^{24}$ equivalent electrons, corresponding to approximately $3\times10^{16}$-$3\times10^{22}$ krypton atoms after division by 36.

NAMES.name: major_radius_of_pellet_path_point
NAMES.short: Major radius (R) coordinate of a point along the pellet injection path, giving the radial distance from the machine toroidal symmetry axis in the cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
The major radius of a pellet path point is the radial distance $R$ from the toroidal symmetry axis to a discrete location along the trajectory of an injected pellet or shattered pellet injector (SPI) fragment, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ increases outward from the machine axis.

Together with [vertical_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_pellet_path_point) (the $Z$ component) and toroidal_angle_of_along_pellet_path (the $\phi$ component), this coordinate fully specifies the three-dimensional position of a point on the pellet or SPI fragment trajectory. The radial coordinate determines how far from the plasma center the injected material deposits fuel or impurity species, directly governing the radial deposition profile.

Pellet path geometry is defined by discrete anchor points — such as the injector exit and, for SPI systems, the shattering position — with the trajectory reconstructed from optical pellet diagnostics or injection geometry specifications. For SPI applications, the shattering-position $R$ value locates where the intact pellet transitions into a dispersing fragment cloud.

Typical values range from about 1.5 m in compact tokamaks to beyond 6 m in large devices, bounded below by the first-wall major radius and above by the outer vessel radius.
NAMES.sign: Positive when $R$ is measured radially outward from the machine toroidal symmetry axis, as defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; $R \geq 0$ for all physically realizable positions.

NAMES.name: neon_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Total number of neon atoms injected as gas during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an electron-equivalent count using the 10 bound electrons of neutral neon.
NAMES.long:
Neon prefill count is the total amount of neon gas introduced before plasma breakdown or current initiation, represented as an electron-equivalent particle count. It is species resolved and prefill-only: it excludes neon injected after breakdown and excludes other gas species used for fueling, wall conditioning, or radiative control.

The electron-equivalent normalization is defined from the injected neutral-neon atom count:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}\,N_{\mathrm{atom}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the neon prefill count, $N_{\mathrm{atom}}^{\mathrm{Ne,prefill}}$ is the number of injected neon atoms during the prefill interval, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}=10$ is the atomic number of neon. This convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition; it is not a statement that the gas is fully ionized during the prefill phase.

In practice, the injected atom count is obtained from calibrated gas-injection measurements such as valve throughput, pressure-volume-temperature accounting, or mass-flow integration over the prefill time window. The electron-equivalent count allows gas quantities for different species to be compared on a common atomic-electron basis while preserving the species identity.

Typical values are scenario and device dependent. Neon prefill may be zero when not used; nonzero values in tokamak applications can span roughly $10^{18}$-$10^{22}$ electron-equivalent counts, with larger values possible for large vacuum volumes or deliberately high-quantity gas-puff scenarios.

NAMES.name: neon_source_rate
NAMES.subject: neon
NAMES.short: Instantaneous injection rate of neon gas into the plasma vessel, expressed in equivalent electrons per second.
NAMES.long: The neon source rate quantifies the instantaneous rate at which neon gas is introduced into the plasma vessel through gas injection systems. Each neon atom (atomic number $Z = 10$) contributes 10 equivalent electrons to the count, so the source rate equals 10 times the atomic injection rate expressed in atoms per second. Neon seeding is widely applied in fusion devices to control edge radiation and protect plasma-facing components from excessive heat loads, and is also employed in disruption mitigation scenarios requiring rapid radiative cooling. The source rate is inferred from calibrated flow controllers or gas injection valve diagnostics, with values ranging from $10^{20}$ to $10^{23}$ s$^{-1}$ depending on the seeding scenario. Integrating this rate over time yields the [accumulated neon count](name:accumulated_neon_count). Analogous injection rates for other species include [nitrogen_source_rate](name:nitrogen_source_rate) and [oxygen_source_rate](name:oxygen_source_rate), which follow the same equivalent-electron convention.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neon gas is being injected into the plasma vessel.

NAMES.name: net_power_of_plant_system
NAMES.short: Net electrical power of a plant system, equal to generated electrical power minus internal operational electrical consumption within the same system boundary.
NAMES.long:
Net electrical power of a plant system is the algebraic electrical power delivered by that system after subtracting the electrical power it consumes for its own operation. It indicates whether the chosen system boundary is a net source or net sink of electricity at a given operating condition.

For a defined plant-system boundary, the net power is

$$
P_\mathrm{net} = P_\mathrm{elec,gen} - P_\mathrm{elec,cons}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{net}$, $P_\mathrm{elec,gen}$, and $P_\mathrm{elec,cons}$ are electrical powers in W evaluated over the same time interval. $P_\mathrm{elec,gen}$ is the electrical power produced within the boundary, such as generator-terminal or power-conversion output, and $P_\mathrm{elec,cons}$ is the operational electrical power drawn by equipment inside the same boundary.

In practice, this quantity is computed from electrical metering or plant power-accounting models by summing generation feeds and subtracting allocated internal loads such as pumps, compressors, cryogenic equipment, control systems, power-conversion auxiliaries, and other parasitic consumers. The system boundary must be applied consistently: loads outside the boundary are excluded, while recirculating power and auxiliary loads inside the boundary are included. During startup, shutdown, standby, or operation of systems without local generation, the net power can be negative.

Typical values depend strongly on the boundary. Purely consuming plant systems are often about -1e3 to -1e8 W, large balance-of-plant or power-conversion systems can range from near 0 W to 1e9 W, and whole-plant net electrical output for power-plant-scale devices is commonly of order 1e8-2e9 W. Values near 0 W indicate that internal electrical consumption nearly balances local electrical generation.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the system exports electrical power across its boundary after subtracting internal operational consumption.

NAMES.name: oxygen_source_rate
NAMES.subject: oxygen
NAMES.short: Instantaneous rate at which oxygen gas is injected into the plasma vessel, expressed as the equivalent number of bound electrons carried by the injected oxygen atoms or molecules per second.
NAMES.long:
Oxygen source rate is the instantaneous input of oxygen gas into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate. The equivalent-electron convention counts eight electrons per oxygen atom, so the quantity tracks the injected oxygen inventory on the same counting basis as total neutral-gas injection rates rather than the instantaneous plasma electron source after ionization.

The relation between the equivalent-electron source rate and the injected neutral oxygen flow is

$$
S_\mathrm{O} = 8\,\dot{N}_\mathrm{O} = 16\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}_2} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{O},e}}{dt}
$$

where $S_\mathrm{O}$ is the oxygen source rate in equivalent electrons per second, $\dot{N}_\mathrm{O}$ is the rate of injected oxygen atoms, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}_2}$ is the rate of injected oxygen molecules, and $N_{\mathrm{O},e}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count. For mixed atomic and molecular gas, contributions are summed with eight equivalent electrons per oxygen nucleus.

In practice, $S_\mathrm{O}$ is computed from calibrated gas-handling signals such as mass-flow-controller demand, reservoir pressure drop, or piezoelectric valve opening together with gas temperature and conductance calibration. Its time integral gives [accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection), and it contributes to the aggregate [electron_source_rate_due_to_injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) along with other injected species such as [hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), [nitrogen_source_rate](name:nitrogen_source_rate), and [neon_source_rate](name:neon_source_rate). Oxygen injection is commonly used for impurity seeding, radiative-power control, radiative mantle formation, and divertor detachment studies; the subsequent ionization balance is a plasma response, not part of this injection-rate definition.

Typical controlled oxygen injection rates are about $10^{19}-10^{22}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ in equivalent-electron units. Small calibration puffs or wall-conditioning flows can be below $10^{19}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$, while large impurity puffs in high-density plasmas may approach or exceed $10^{22}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

NAMES.name: propane_prefill_count
NAMES.subject: propane
NAMES.short: Total propane (C3H8) introduced during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count using 26 electrons per propane molecule.
NAMES.long:
Propane prefill count is the accumulated amount of propane introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. A propane molecule, C$_3$H$_8$, contains $3 \times 6 + 8 \times 1 = 26$ electrons, so each injected molecule contributes 26 to this count.

The accumulated prefill count is defined from the propane molecular flow integrated over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}} = 26\,N_{\mathrm{mol}} = 26 \int_{t_{\mathrm{start}}}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{mol}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{mol}}$ is the dimensionless count of propane molecules injected during prefill, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mol}}$ is the propane molecular flow rate in molecules s$^{-1}$, and $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start time and breakdown time in seconds.

In practice, the value is obtained from the propane gas-injection accounting over the prefill interval, using the inferred or measured molecular throughput and the gas-species conversion factor. It contributes to the total prefill inventory [prefill_count](name:accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection) and is directly comparable with other prefill gas counts because all are expressed on the same equivalent-electron scale.

The physical range is $N_{\mathrm{eq}} \ge 0$, with $N_{\mathrm{eq}} = 0$ when no propane is introduced during prefill. No universal numerical range is implied: values depend strongly on vessel volume, prefill pressure target, gas-line calibration, and pulse scenario, and may vary by many orders of magnitude between devices and operating regimes.

NAMES.name: radial_velocity_of_pellet
NAMES.short: Major-radius component of the shattered pellet center-of-mass velocity in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
NAMES.long:
Radial velocity of a pellet is the component of the pellet center-of-mass velocity along the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It quantifies motion of the pellet material center of mass toward or away from the symmetry axis, separate from toroidal and vertical motion.

The radial component is obtained by projecting the center-of-mass velocity onto the local radial basis vector:

$$
v_R = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{cm} \cdot \hat{R}
$$
