NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged parallel component of the fast-particle pressure tensor for suprathermal particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits. It measures the field-aligned kinetic pressure carried by fast particles whose passing motion is opposite to the plasma-current direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the component of the suprathermal-particle pressure tensor projected along the local magnetic field, restricted to particles on counter-passing guiding-center orbits. Counter-passing particles are passing particles whose orbit motion is opposite to the plasma-current direction. Because this pressure component is formed from the squared parallel velocity, it is a non-negative scalar even though the selected orbit class is direction-dependent.

For a kinetic distribution, the flux-surface-averaged quantity can be written as:

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{counter}} = \left\langle \sum_s \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{counter}}} m_s v_\parallel^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v \right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component along the local magnetic field, $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the non-thermal distribution function, $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{counter}}$ is the counter-passing part of velocity or orbit space, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes averaging over a magnetic flux surface.

In practice it is computed from a reconstructed or modeled fast-particle distribution by classifying guiding-center orbits into co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped populations, then taking the second velocity moment parallel to the magnetic field over the counter-passing subset. It is commonly compared with the corresponding perpendicular component, [perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), to characterize pressure anisotropy of the counter-passing fast-particle population.

Typical values range from less than 1 Pa in weakly heated or edge regions to 100-10000 Pa in strongly heated core plasmas, depending on injected or fusion-born fast-particle density, energy, pitch-angle distribution, and slowing-down state.

NAMES.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
NAMES.short: Field-aligned component of the electric current density driven by frictional momentum exchange between plasma ions and background neutral particles in partially ionized edge and divertor plasmas.
NAMES.long:
In partially ionized plasmas — found in the edge, scrape-off layer, and divertor regions of a tokamak — collisions between plasma ions and coexisting neutral atoms transfer momentum between the two fluids, producing an ion-neutral friction force $\mathbf{R}_{in} = m_i n_i \nu_{in}(\mathbf{v}_n - \mathbf{v}_i)$, where $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, $\nu_{in}$ is the ion-neutral collision frequency, and $\mathbf{v}_i$, $\mathbf{v}_n$ are the ion and neutral fluid velocities respectively. This friction force drives an electric current whose full vector form is given by [current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction); the present quantity is the projection of that vector onto the local magnetic field direction.

The parallel component is defined as:

$$
j_{\parallel,\text{in}} = \mathbf{j}_{\text{in}} \cdot \hat{b}
$$

where $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/B$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field and $\mathbf{j}_{\text{in}}$ is the full ion-neutral friction current density vector.

This component enters the parallel momentum balance and the generalized Ohm's law for partially ionized plasmas, and is most significant in regions of high neutral density such as the divertor target and scrape-off layer. It is computed from fluid or kinetic simulations of edge plasmas that resolve neutral transport. The complete set of geometric projections includes [radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), [poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), [toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction), and [vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion-neutral friction current flows in the direction of the magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.short: Effective diffusion coefficient for ion fluid momentum parallel to magnetic field lines in the edge plasma. It quantifies diffusive, rather than convective, spreading of parallel momentum.
NAMES.long:
Parallel edge-plasma momentum diffusivity is the scalar coefficient that relates gradients of ion parallel momentum density to diffusive transport along magnetic field lines in the edge plasma. It describes local momentum spreading and is distinct from parallel convective transport, such as [parallel_ion_momentum_convection_velocity](name:parallel_ion_momentum_convection_velocity) and [parallel_ion_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:parallel_ion_state_momentum_convection_velocity).

The diffusive part of the parallel momentum flux is commonly written using field-line arclength $s$:

$$
J_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{edge}} \frac{\partial M_\parallel}{\partial s}
$$

where $J_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of ion parallel momentum with units kg m^-1 s^-2, $D_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{edge}}$ is the parallel edge-plasma momentum diffusivity with units m^2 s^-1, $M_\parallel$ is ion parallel momentum density with units kg m^-2 s^-1, and $s$ is distance in meters increasing along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. A positive $J_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ denotes flux in the $+\hat{b}$ direction; for positive diffusivity the minus sign gives transport down the gradient of $M_\parallel$.

In transport modeling this coefficient is prescribed or inferred as the multiplier of the parallel-gradient term in the ion momentum balance. It may be used together with a separate parallel convection velocity to distinguish diffusive smoothing of momentum from advective carrying of momentum by a directed flow.

Representative effective values in edge-plasma applications are commonly broad, about 10^2-10^6 m^2 s^-1. Lower values, around 1-10^2 m^2 s^-1, correspond to weak parallel momentum smoothing, while values near 10^4-10^6 m^2 s^-1 represent rapid equilibration along field lines over edge connection lengths.

NAMES.name: parallel_electric_field
NAMES.short: Component of the electric field projected onto the local magnetic field direction, driving ohmic current and governing resistive magnetic-flux diffusion along field lines.
NAMES.long:
The parallel electric field $E_\parallel = \mathbf{E} \cdot \hat{b}$, where $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, is the electric-force component acting on charged particles moving along field lines. It is the primary driver of Ohmic (inductive) current and enters the resistive magnetic-flux diffusion equation that governs the evolution of the poloidal flux profile.

In one-dimensional transport modeling the quantity is commonly represented as the flux-surface average $\langle \mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} \rangle / B_0$, where $B_0$ is a reference magnetic field value. It satisfies the parallel Ohm's law:

$$
E_\parallel = \eta_\parallel j_\parallel + E_{\parallel,\mathrm{ni}}
$$

where $\eta_\parallel$ is the parallel (Spitzer) resistivity, $j_\parallel$ is the parallel current density linked to [parallel_ohmic_current_density](name:parallel_ohmic_current_density), and $E_{\parallel,\mathrm{ni}}$ collects non-inductive contributions from wave-driven and neoclassical sources.

The field is inferred by solving the current-diffusion equation constrained by loop-voltage and external-coil boundary measurements, or computed self-consistently in transport codes. Typical core magnitudes in Ohmic discharges range from 0.01–1 V/m, rising to several V/m in the edge and scrape-off layer; the boundary value at the separatrix is described by [parallel_flux_surface_averaged_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary](name:parallel_flux_surface_averaged_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary).
NAMES.sign: Positive when $\mathbf{E} \cdot \mathbf{B} > 0$, i.e., when the electric field has a component in the same direction as the magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Parallel electron energy diffusivity is the effective field-aligned diffusion coefficient for conductive transport of electron thermal energy. It relates electron heat flux along the magnetic field to the electron-temperature gradient in the electron energy equation.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron energy diffusivity, usually denoted $\chi_{e,\parallel}$, quantifies conductive spreading of electron thermal energy along magnetic field lines. Because magnetized electrons move much more freely along the magnetic field than across it, this coefficient is typically far larger than radial or poloidal electron energy diffusivities.

A common local closure for the field-aligned conductive heat flux is:

$$
q_{e,\parallel} = - n_e \chi_{e,\parallel} \nabla_{\parallel} T_e
$$

where $q_{e,\parallel}$ is the electron conductive energy flux along the magnetic field, $n_e$ is electron density, $\nabla_{\parallel}=\hat{b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, and $T_e$ is electron temperature expressed as energy per particle. If $T_e$ is expressed in eV, conversion to W m^-2 requires multiplication by the elementary charge. The minus sign means that a positive diffusivity drives heat from higher toward lower electron temperature.

This quantity is usually inferred or prescribed in transport modeling rather than measured directly. In collisional regimes it is related to Braginskii or Spitzer-Härm parallel electron heat conduction and scales strongly with temperature, approximately as $T_e^{5/2}$, while weakly collisional plasmas may require nonlocal or flux-limited closures. Effective values can also include unresolved turbulent or kinetic effects.

Typical classical estimates are about 10^6-10^8 m^2 s^-1 in 10-100 eV edge plasmas and can exceed 10^10 m^2 s^-1 in keV core plasmas. Phenomenological or flux-limited models may use lower effective values to represent finite mean-free-path effects or numerical regularization.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Scalar component of the electron energy flux density parallel to the local magnetic field. It is positive for transport in the direction of the magnetic field and negative for transport in the opposite direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron energy flux is the field-aligned scalar component of the electron energy flux density. It represents the rate at which electron energy crosses a unit area whose normal is parallel to the local magnetic-field direction, including conductive, convective, and other modeled electron-energy transport contributions as appropriate.

The parallel component is defined by projecting the electron energy flux density vector onto the magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
q_{e,\parallel} = \mathbf{Q}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $q_{e,\parallel}$ is the parallel electron energy flux in W m$^{-2}$, $\mathbf{Q}_e$ is the electron energy flux density vector in W m$^{-2}$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic flux density in T, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is a dimensionless unit vector along $\mathbf{B}$. In collisional fluid descriptions, a common conductive contribution is proportional to $-\kappa_{e,\parallel}\nabla_{\parallel}T_e$, while an enthalpy or convective contribution is commonly proportional to $n_e T_e v_{e,\parallel}$; the reported value is the signed total parallel electron-energy flux used by the transport model.

This quantity is computed in electron energy transport calculations from the modeled heat-flux closure, particle flow, temperature gradient, and magnetic geometry. It is the energy-flux analog of [parallel_electron_particle_flux](name:parallel_electron_particle_flux) and complements transverse components such as [radial_electron_energy_flux](name:radial_electron_energy_flux) when decomposing electron energy transport relative to the magnetic field.

Representative magnitudes are highly regime dependent. Parallel electron energy fluxes in confined or edge plasma transport studies can range from about $10^3$-$10^6$ W m$^{-2}$ in weakly driven regions to $10^6$-$10^8$ W m$^{-2}$ or more along scrape-off-layer field lines connected to strong exhaust power.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron energy flux is directed along $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

NAMES.name: parallel_electron_velocity
NAMES.subject: electron
NAMES.short: Parallel electron velocity is the electron-fluid bulk velocity projected along the local magnetic-field direction. It is the field-aligned component of electron flow and contributes to parallel particle flux and parallel current density.
NAMES.long:
Parallel electron velocity is the component of the electron fluid bulk flow along the local magnetic field. It describes field-aligned electron motion, not a geometric radial, poloidal, or toroidal projection.

The defining projection is

$$
v_{e\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{e\parallel}$ is in m.s^-1, $\mathbf{v}_e$ is the electron fluid velocity vector in m.s^-1, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the dimensionless unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field in T.

The associated parallel electron particle flux is $\Gamma_{e\parallel}=n_e v_{e\parallel}$, where $n_e$ is the electron number density in m^-3 and $\Gamma_{e\parallel}$ is in m^-2.s^-1. The parallel current density satisfies $j_\parallel=\sum_i Z_i e n_i v_{i\parallel}-e n_e v_{e\parallel}$, with $j_\parallel$ in A.m^-2, $e$ in C, $n_i$ and $n_e$ in m^-3, $v_{i\parallel}$ and $v_{e\parallel}$ in m.s^-1, and $Z_i$ dimensionless. Under quasi-neutrality, $n_e=\sum_i Z_i n_i$, this can be written as $j_\parallel=e n_e(\bar{v}_{i\parallel}-v_{e\parallel})$, where $\bar{v}_{i\parallel}=\sum_i Z_i n_i v_{i\parallel}/n_e$ is the charge-density-weighted ion parallel velocity; for one ion species, $\bar{v}_{i\parallel}=v_{i\parallel}$.

Direct diagnostic access to this velocity is limited. It is commonly inferred from parallel current density, ion parallel flow, electron density, or density-normalized parallel electron particle flux, and it is computed in fluid or kinetic models as the first velocity-space moment of the electron distribution along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$. It is coupled to the parallel electric field through the parallel component of generalized Ohm's law.

Typical magnitudes are 10^4-10^6 m.s^-1 in confined and edge tokamak plasmas, depending on current density, collisionality, and connection length. These flows are usually below the electron thermal speed, although sheath-connected edge plasmas can support large field-aligned electron streaming.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the electron bulk flow is directed along the local magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_ion_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Fast ion pressure parallel to the local magnetic field is the suprathermal ion contribution to the pressure tensor projected along the field direction. It is combined over charge states and represents the parallel velocity spread of non-thermal ions.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast ion pressure is the component of the fast-ion pressure tensor associated with random particle motion along the local magnetic field. It describes the anisotropic pressure contribution from suprathermal ions such as beam ions, radio-frequency-accelerated ions, and fusion-born alpha particles, and it differs from perpendicular fast ion pressure when the fast-ion velocity distribution is pitch-angle anisotropic.

Using the fast-ion pressure tensor, the defining projection is

$$
p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf{b}} \cdot \mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \sum_a m_a \int (v_\parallel - u_{\parallel,a})^2 f_a(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the local unit vector along the magnetic field, $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion pressure tensor, $a$ indexes the included ion species or charge states, $m_a$ is the ion mass, $f_a$ is the fast-ion distribution function, $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, and $u_{\parallel,a}$ is the corresponding mean parallel velocity.

In practice this quantity is obtained from kinetic fast-ion distribution functions produced by transport, Fokker-Planck, or orbit-following calculations, often constrained by neutron emission, fast-ion D-alpha, neutral-particle analysis, gamma-ray emission, or collective Thomson scattering. If only a scalar fast-ion pressure is available, assumptions about velocity-space anisotropy are required; for an isotropic fast-ion population, $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ equals the perpendicular component and the scalar pressure is $p_{\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$.

Typical values range from 0.1-10^3 Pa in edge or weak-tail regions, 10^3-10^5 Pa in heated tokamak cores, and up to several 10^5 Pa in high-power auxiliary-heated or burning-plasma regimes.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_ion_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the fast-ion pressure for a specific ion charge state, measuring suprathermal ion stress along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast-ion state pressure is the diagonal component of the fast-ion pressure tensor along the local magnetic field for one ion charge state. It represents the kinetic stress carried by suprathermal, non-Maxwellian ions and is generally distinct from the perpendicular component when the fast-ion distribution is anisotropic.

For a gyrotropic fast-ion distribution, the parallel component is the second velocity-space moment along the magnetic-field direction:

$$
p_{\mathrm{fast},s,\parallel} = m_s \int (v_\parallel - u_{s,\parallel})^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the ion mass for charge state $s$, $v_\parallel$ is the particle velocity component parallel to the local magnetic field, $u_{s,\parallel}$ is the mean parallel velocity of that fast-ion state, and $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the fast-ion distribution function. With $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ expressed as number density per velocity-space volume, with units $s^3 m^{-6}$, the integral gives pressure in Pa.

This quantity is computed from kinetic descriptions of energetic ions, such as Fokker-Planck, orbit-following, Monte Carlo, or reduced moment models, and may be constrained by diagnostics sensitive to suprathermal ions, including neutron emission, neutral-particle analysis, fast-ion light emission, gamma-ray emission, and magnetic-equilibrium effects. It is used with the perpendicular fast-ion state pressure to represent anisotropic energetic-particle contributions to force balance, transport, and stability.

Typical values range from less than 1 Pa in weakly populated edge or scrape-off-layer regions to 10^3-10^5 Pa in strongly heated core plasmas. Values depend on fast-ion density, birth energy, slowing-down time, pitch-angle anisotropy, and charge-state population.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_neutral_state_pressure
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the kinetic pressure tensor for fast (suprathermal) neutral particles in a specified internal quantum or excitation state, directed along the local magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
The parallel fast neutral state pressure is the field-aligned component of the kinetic pressure tensor for suprathermal neutral particles occupying a resolved internal quantum or excitation state $s$. It captures the anisotropic pressure that fast neutrals — particles whose energy significantly exceeds the local thermal equilibrium — exert along the magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$, and is the state-resolved counterpart of [parallel_fast_neutral_pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure).

The quantity is defined as the second central velocity moment of the state-resolved fast-neutral distribution function $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{v})$ projected onto the magnetic field unit vector $\hat{b}$:

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast},s} = m_n \int \left(v_\parallel - u_{\parallel,s}\right)^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $v_\parallel = \mathbf{v} \cdot \hat{b}$ is the velocity component along the local field direction, and $u_{\parallel,s}$ is the mean parallel flow speed of neutrals in state $s$.

This quantity arises primarily in edge plasma and scrape-off layer modeling, where charge exchange and recycling processes generate suprathermal neutrals with inherently anisotropic velocity distributions. Resolving by internal state allows neutral transport models to track pressure contributions from distinct excitation or ionization levels separately. The perpendicular counterpart is [perpendicular_fast_neutral_state_pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_state_pressure); combining the two components via $P = (P_\parallel + 2P_\perp)/3$ yields the scalar isotropic fast neutral state pressure.
NAMES.sign: Positive when fast neutral particles in state $s$ carry a non-zero parallel velocity spread about their mean flow along the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_particle_energy
NAMES.subject: particle
NAMES.short: Total parallel kinetic energy of fast (suprathermal) particles, integrated over the plasma volume.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the part of the kinetic energy of the suprathermal particle population associated with motion along the local magnetic field. It is the field-aligned counterpart of perpendicular fast-particle energy and excludes the perpendicular gyromotion contribution.

For a distribution-function definition, the parallel contribution is obtained from the field-aligned velocity moment of the fast-particle distribution:

$$
W_{\parallel,f} = \sum_s \int_V \int \frac{1}{2} m_s v_\parallel^2 f_{f,s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v\, dV
$$

where $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass, $v_\parallel$ is the velocity component along the local magnetic field, $f_{f,s}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, and $dV$ is a physical volume element in m^3. If the same moment is represented by a parallel pressure $p_{\parallel,f}$, then $p_{\parallel,f}$ has units Pa = J m^-3 and the one-degree-of-freedom contribution is $W_{\parallel,f}=\frac{1}{2}\int_V p_{\parallel,f}\,dV$.

In practice this quantity is computed from fast-particle distribution functions, kinetic transport calculations, or pressure-moment reconstructions constrained by heating, slowing-down, and loss physics. It is sensitive to pitch-angle anisotropy: particles born or accelerated mainly along the magnetic field increase the parallel share, while strongly trapped or perpendicular populations shift energy toward the perpendicular contribution.

Representative values are highly device and scenario dependent, spanning roughly 10^3-10^7 J in many auxiliary-heated tokamak plasmas and reaching 10^7-10^8 J in large high-power or burning-plasma scenarios. The fraction of total fast-particle energy in the parallel degree of freedom depends on source geometry, collisional pitch-angle scattering, and confinement losses.

NAMES.name: parallel_fast_particle_pressure
NAMES.subject: particle
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the fast-particle pressure tensor, formed from the second suprathermal velocity moment along the magnetic field. It includes co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit populations unless an orbit-resolved quantity is specified.
NAMES.long:
Parallel fast-particle pressure is the component of the kinetic pressure tensor associated with nonthermal particles moving parallel to the local magnetic field. It measures the parallel momentum flux of the suprathermal distribution and includes co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped orbit populations unless one of those populations is treated separately.

The kinetic definition is the parallel second velocity moment of the fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{f,\parallel}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a,o} m_a \int v_\parallel^2 f_{f,a,o}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $a$ labels particle species, $o$ labels orbit classes, $m_a$ is the particle mass, $f_{f,a,o}$ is the fast-particle distribution function, and $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{b}$ with $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. The integral is over velocity space; for a species-restricted fast-particle population the sum over $a$ is omitted. If directed fast-particle flow is removed separately, $v_\parallel$ in the pressure moment is replaced by the corresponding parallel peculiar velocity.

In practice this quantity is obtained by integrating reconstructed or modeled fast-particle distribution functions. Neutral-particle analysis, fast-ion D-alpha spectroscopy, neutron or gamma diagnostics, collective Thomson scattering, and magnetic fluctuation measurements can constrain the distribution, while Fokker-Planck, Monte Carlo, gyrokinetic, or transport calculations commonly provide the full moment. A flux-surface-averaged form is obtained by averaging this local moment over the chosen magnetic flux surface.

Together with [perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), it characterizes fast-particle pressure anisotropy. For an isotropic fast population, $p_{f,\parallel}=p_{f,\perp}$ and the scalar fast_particle_pressure is $(p_{f,\parallel}+2p_{f,\perp})/3$; departures from this relation affect equilibrium force balance and can modify Alfvénic and pressure-anisotropy-driven modes.

Typical values range from 10^2-10^5 Pa in the core of auxiliary-heated tokamak plasmas, depending on heating power, slowing-down time, particle energy, and confinement. Edge and scrape-off-layer values are often much lower, while high-performance or alpha-particle-dominated plasmas can approach several 10^5 Pa.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Field-aligned diffusivity for the parallel momentum of ions in a specified ionization (charge) state. It is the kinematic transport coefficient that, multiplied by the charge-state mass density, relates the down-gradient parallel momentum flux to the gradient of the parallel flow velocity along the magnetic field in a Fick-law closure.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusivity is the scalar kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive transport of field-aligned momentum carried by ions in a specified ionization state along the magnetic field. It encapsulates the effective momentum mixing produced by neoclassical collisional viscosity and anomalous turbulent processes for that charge state.

In a Fick-law closure, the field-aligned diffusive flux of parallel momentum is proportional to the charge-state mass density and the gradient of the parallel flow velocity:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel,z} = -\, m_i n_z D_{\parallel,z} \frac{\partial v_{\parallel,z}}{\partial s}
$$

where $\Pi_{\parallel,z}$ is the field-aligned diffusive flux of parallel momentum (in kg m^-1 s^-2), $m_i$ is the ion mass (in kg), $n_z$ is the number density of the charge state (in m^-3), $v_{\parallel,z}$ is the mean parallel flow velocity (in m s^-1), $s$ is arc length measured along the magnetic field line (in m), and $D_{\parallel,z}$ is this diffusivity. The product $m_i n_z D_{\parallel,z}$ has units of dynamic viscosity, so the closure is consistent with the accepted parallel-momentum diffusion coefficient definition that acts on the velocity gradient rather than on the momentum-density gradient.

This coefficient is inferred from parallel momentum-balance analysis using measured or reconstructed charge-state densities, flow velocities, momentum sources, and non-diffusive contributions such as convection and residual stress. Charge-state resolution is important for impurities, where ionization, recombination, collisional coupling, and friction with the main ions make the effective momentum transport state dependent.

Values are strongly model and regime dependent; effective field-aligned momentum diffusivities span a wide range from order 1 m^2 s^-1 in cold, collisional edge regions to much larger values in hot, weakly collisional core plasmas.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the diffusivity drives the parallel momentum flux down the gradient of the parallel flow velocity.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_charge_state
NAMES.short: Particle flux density of ions in a specified charge state projected onto the local magnetic-field direction. It is the signed rate at which that charge-state population streams along the field per unit area.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion charge-state particle flux is the signed particle flux density of ions in one ionization stage resolved along the local magnetic field direction. It describes field-aligned streaming of that charge-state population and is a charge-state-resolved contribution to [parallel_ion_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_particle_flux).

For charge state $z$, the common fluid definition is:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,z} = n_z v_{\parallel,z}
$$

where $n_z$ is the number density of ions in charge state $z$ in $m^{-3}$, and $v_{\parallel,z}$ is their mean velocity component along $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ in $m\,s^{-1}$. The product has units of particle flux density, $m^{-2}\,s^{-1}$.

In charge-state particle balance, this quantity enters through the field-aligned divergence term, commonly written inline as $\nabla \cdot (\Gamma_{\parallel,z}\hat{b})$, together with perpendicular transport and sources or sinks from ionization, recombination, charge exchange, and external fueling. It is usually computed from kinetic distribution moments or fluid density and flow variables, and may be constrained indirectly using spectroscopy, charge-exchange measurements, and transport reconstruction.

Typical magnitudes vary widely with species, charge state, confinement region, and collisionality. Trace impurity charge states in the confined plasma may be below $10^{18}$ m^-2.s^-1, while edge, scrape-off-layer, and divertor charge states with strong field-aligned flows commonly reach $10^{20}-10^{24}$ m^-2.s^-1.
NAMES.sign: Positive when ions in the specified charge state flow in the direction of the local magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$, equivalently along $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Effective local diffusivity for ion thermal-energy transport along the magnetic field. It applies to a specified ion species when the transported energy is species resolved, and to a total-ion effective channel when ion energies are summed.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion energy diffusivity is the local effective diffusion coefficient that relates field-aligned gradients of ion thermal energy to the conductive part of the ion heat flux. It characterizes how rapidly ion thermal energy is smoothed along magnetic field lines; for a species-resolved energy variable it is species-specific, while for a summed ion energy variable it is an aggregate total-ion coefficient. It is a local transport coefficient, not a line, flux-surface, or volume average unless an averaging operation is explicitly part of the physical model.

A common Fick's-law closure for the conductive field-aligned energy flux is:

$$
q_{E_i,\parallel} = -\chi_{E_i,\parallel}\,\nabla_\parallel w_i
$$

where $q_{E_i,\parallel}$ is the scalar parallel ion heat-flux density in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ and is positive for energy transport along $\hat{b}$, $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local magnetic field, $\chi_{E_i,\parallel}$ is the parallel ion energy diffusivity in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$, $w_i$ is the local ion thermal energy density in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and $\nabla_\parallel=\hat{b}\cdot\nabla$ is the derivative along the magnetic field in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. The minus sign means that the conductive heat flux is down the field-aligned energy-density gradient. For a single ion species $s$, $w_s$ may be written as $(3/2)n_s\mathcal{T}_s$, with $n_s$ in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $\mathcal{T}_s$ the ion temperature expressed as energy per particle in joules; if $T_s$ is given in eV, then $\mathcal{T}_s=eT_s$, where $e$ is the elementary charge. For total-ion energy, $w_i$ represents the summed thermal energy density over the ion species included in the model.

This coefficient is usually inferred or prescribed rather than measured directly. It may be obtained from transport analysis, from collisional or fluid closure estimates, or by fitting field-aligned heat transport in a reduced model; the interpretation depends on the thermal-energy variable to which the coefficient is applied.

Typical magnitudes are strongly regime and model dependent. Collisional estimates scale roughly with ion thermal speed squared times the ion-ion collision time; representative effective values can range from $10^2-10^6\ \mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$ in cold, collisional edge or scrape-off-layer plasmas to $10^8-10^{11}\ \mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$ in hot, weakly collisional core plasmas.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Projection of the ion energy flux vector onto the local magnetic field direction, giving the field-aligned component of ion thermal and kinetic energy transport.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion energy flux quantifies the rate at which ion energy is transported per unit area along the magnetic field direction $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. Field-aligned ion transport dominates cross-field transport in the collisional edge and scrape-off layer, making this quantity a key term in the parallel ion energy balance and a primary driver of heat loads at divertor targets.

From Braginskii fluid closure, the parallel energy flux density combines convective and conductive contributions:

$$
q_{\parallel,i} = \frac{5}{2} n_i T_i v_{\parallel,i} - \kappa_{\parallel,i} \nabla_\parallel T_i
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $T_i$ is the ion temperature in energy units, $v_{\parallel,i}$ is the parallel ion fluid velocity, and $\kappa_{\parallel,i}$ is the parallel ion thermal conductivity. The first term represents enthalpy convection and the second is Fourier conduction along the field.

This flux appears as a divergence contribution in the ion energy conservation equation and is the primary carrier of ion thermal energy toward divertor targets in attached plasma regimes. For the charge-state-resolved counterpart, see [parallel_ion_state_energy_flux](name:parallel_ion_state_energy_flux); the species-summed total is [parallel_total_ion_energy_flux](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_flux). The electron analog is [parallel_electron_energy_flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux) and the neutral contribution is [parallel_neutral_energy_flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux).
NAMES.sign: Positive when energy is transported in the direction of the magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Inverse relaxation rate for decay of the field-aligned component of bulk ion momentum. It is an effective aggregate over ion species or charge states, with damping mainly from Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion momentum damping rate is the inverse timescale for relaxation of the bulk ion momentum component along the local magnetic field. It represents the net damping experienced by the combined ion population after summing over ion species or charge states, rather than the damping of one resolved ion state alone.

It is defined through the damping contribution to the parallel ion momentum balance:

$$
S_{\parallel i}^{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{\parallel i} M_{\parallel i}, \qquad M_{\parallel i} = \sum_\alpha m_\alpha n_\alpha u_{\parallel\alpha}
$$

where $\nu_{\parallel i}$ is the bulk parallel ion momentum damping rate in $s^{-1}$, $S_{\parallel i}^{\mathrm{damp}}$ is the parallel momentum sink density in $N\,m^{-3}$, equivalently $kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-2}$, and $M_{\parallel i}$ is the bulk parallel ion momentum density in $kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}$. The index $\alpha$ labels ion species or charge states, with mass $m_\alpha$ in $kg$, density $n_\alpha$ in $m^{-3}$, and parallel flow velocity $u_{\parallel\alpha}$ in $m\,s^{-1}$. The minus sign means that a positive damping rate reduces the existing bulk parallel momentum.

In transport modeling this coefficient is usually computed from collisional and neoclassical momentum relaxation mechanisms, including Coulomb collisions, interspecies friction, and neoclassical viscous stresses. Relative to [parallel_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate), the bulk coefficient is the effective rate obtained after summing the state-resolved damped momentum sources: for nonzero net bulk momentum, $\nu_{\parallel i}=-\sum_\alpha S_{\parallel\alpha}^{\mathrm{damp}}/\sum_\alpha M_{\parallel\alpha}$. If each ion state is linearly damped with $S_{\parallel\alpha}^{\mathrm{damp}}=-\nu_{\parallel\alpha}M_{\parallel\alpha}$, this becomes the corresponding signed momentum-weighted effective rate.

Typical values are highly model and collisionality dependent. In hot confined plasmas, representative rates are often 0.1-10^5 s^-1; in colder, denser, or high-collisionality regions they can reach 10^5-10^7 s^-1. Values near 0 s^-1 indicate negligible modeled damping or an intentionally omitted damping channel.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Field-aligned effective diffusion coefficient governing the diffusive redistribution of momentum within the bulk ion population along magnetic field lines.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion momentum diffusivity $D_{\parallel}^i$ is the field-aligned component of the effective ion momentum diffusion coefficient, characterizing how diffusive processes — viscous and turbulent — transport ion momentum along the magnetic field direction $\hat{b}$. It is the ion-specific, species-summed analog of [parallel_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity), which covers the total plasma momentum, and differs from the charge-state-resolved [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) by integrating contributions across all ionization states of the ion population.

The coefficient enters the ion parallel momentum balance through a Fick-law flux relation:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel}^{\mathrm{mom}} = -D_{\parallel}^i \, \nabla_{\parallel}(m_i n_i u_{\parallel})
$$

where $m_i$ is the mean ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, $u_{\parallel}$ is the parallel ion fluid velocity, and $\nabla_{\parallel} = \hat{b} \cdot \nabla$ is the gradient along the unit magnetic field vector $\hat{b}$.

This coefficient is used in fluid transport models of the edge and scrape-off-layer plasma, where parallel momentum flows connect the upstream midplane to the divertor targets. The parent quantity [ion_momentum_diffusivity](name:ion_momentum_diffusivity) aggregates contributions from all field directions, while $D_{\parallel}^i$ isolates the field-aligned channel.

Typical values in tokamak edge plasma transport models range from 0.1 to 100 m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, with upper values dominated by turbulent and neoclassical viscosity in the scrape-off layer.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the total ion particle flux density along the local magnetic field direction, aggregated over all charge states of the ion species.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion particle flux $\Gamma_{\parallel,i}$ quantifies the net flow of ions per unit area per unit time along the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, summed over all charge states of the ion species. It enters the ion density continuity equation as the divergence term governing parallel transport, and is the dominant particle transport channel along open magnetic field lines in the scrape-off layer and divertor regions.

The defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,i} = n_i \, v_{\parallel,i}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density and $v_{\parallel,i}$ is the component of the ion fluid velocity parallel to $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity is computed in edge and plasma transport models from the fluid momentum balance or by integrating the ion distribution function over the parallel velocity dimension. For charge-state-resolved transport, the counterpart [parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) provides per-charge-state resolution. The analogous quantities for other plasma components are [parallel_electron_particle_flux](name:parallel_electron_particle_flux) and [parallel_neutral_particle_flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux).

Typical magnitudes in the scrape-off layer range from $10^{20}$ to $10^{22}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, with values increasing toward divertor target plates as parallel flow accelerates toward the Bohm condition at the magnetic presheath entrance.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion particle flow is co-directed with the magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Signed field-aligned component of the energy flux density carried by ions in one resolved charge state. It represents the power per unit area transported by that ionization state along the local magnetic-field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel ion-state energy flux is the component of the energy flux density for a specified ion species and charge state along the local magnetic field. It describes how rapidly that ionization state transports energy through a unit area normal to the field-aligned direction.

The field-aligned component is defined by projecting the ion-state energy-flux vector onto the magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
q_{\parallel,i,z} = \mathbf{q}_{E,i,z} \cdot \mathbf{b}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_{E,i,z}$ is the energy flux density of ion species $i$ in charge state $z$, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $q_{\parallel,i,z}$ is expressed in W m$^{-2}$. Depending on the transport model, $\mathbf{q}_{E,i,z}$ may include conductive heat transport, convective enthalpy transport, and kinetic-energy transport associated with directed motion of that ionization state.

In practice this quantity is inferred from transport modeling, fluid or kinetic simulations, or diagnostic-constrained edge and core analyzes. It is commonly related to ion-state density, temperature, flow velocity, temperature gradients along field lines, and collisional exchange with electrons, neutrals, and other ion charge states.

Typical magnitudes span a wide range: about $10^2$-$10^5$ W m$^{-2}$ for weakly transported core impurity charge states, $10^4$-$10^7$ W m$^{-2}$ in edge plasmas, and up to $10^7$-$10^9$ W m$^{-2}$ along scrape-off-layer field lines in high-power discharges.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion-state energy flux is directed along the local magnetic-field direction.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Inverse relaxation time for dissipation of the field-aligned flow momentum of a specific ion charge state, driven by Coulomb collisions and neoclassical viscous stresses.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion state momentum damping rate $\nu_\parallel$ is the inverse time scale at which the magnetic-field-aligned flow momentum of an ion species in a specified charge state is removed by collisional friction, pitch-angle scattering, and neoclassical viscous stresses. It provides charge-state resolution of the parallel momentum sink, distinguishing contributions from individual ionization levels and enabling accurate tracking of impurity momentum balance across species.

The rate enters the parallel component of the ion momentum transport equation as a linear sink:

$$
\frac{\partial u_\parallel}{\partial t} = \cdots - \nu_\parallel \, u_\parallel
$$

where $u_\parallel = \mathbf{u} \cdot \hat{b}$ is the parallel flow velocity of the charge state, $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $\nu_\parallel$ is this damping rate. The parallel component is distinguished from the poloidal and radial projections: see [poloidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:poloidal_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate) and [radial_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:radial_ion_state_momentum_damping_rate). The charge-state-summed counterpart is [parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate), and this quantity is a directional component of [ion_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_state_momentum_damping_rate). The rate is computed from neoclassical transport theory or Fokker–Planck kinetic models as a function of plasma density, temperature, ion charge, and collisionality regime.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the parallel momentum of the ion charge state is being dissipated, corresponding to a damping sink acting to reduce the parallel flow velocity toward zero.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_state_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion_state
NAMES.short: Projection of the mean bulk fluid velocity of ions in a specific charge state onto the local magnetic field direction, resolved per ionization state rather than averaged over all charge states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion state velocity is the scalar projection of the mean bulk flow of an ion population in a specific ionization charge state $Z$ onto the local magnetic field unit vector $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. This charge-state-resolved quantity is distinct from the charge-state-averaged [parallel_ion_velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity), making it essential for impurity transport modeling where individual ionization stages have different density profiles, temperatures, and flow patterns.

The parallel component is defined as:

$$
v_{\parallel,i,Z} = \mathbf{v}_{i,Z} \cdot \hat{b}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{i,Z}$ is the [ion_state_velocity](name:ion_state_velocity) vector for charge state $Z$ and $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This velocity component governs parallel transport of charge-state density along field lines, parallel pressure balance, and inter-species collisional friction forces. It couples dynamically to [parallel_electron_velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity) through the parallel current and ambipolarity constraints, and is structurally analogous to parallel_neutral_state_velocity for the neutral counterpart.

In multi-fluid transport modeling, $v_{\parallel,i,Z}$ is evolved from the charge-state-resolved parallel momentum equation including pressure-gradient driving, collisional friction, and viscous forces. Experimental constraints can be obtained by projecting ion velocity components measured with charge exchange recombination spectroscopy onto $\hat{b}$ when multiple viewing geometries are available.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion bulk flow is directed along $\hat{b}$, co-directional with the magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ion_velocity
NAMES.subject: ion
NAMES.short: Projection of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk flow velocity onto the local magnetic field direction, giving the field-aligned component of the mean ion fluid motion at each plasma location.
NAMES.long:
The parallel ion velocity $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the component of the charge-state-averaged ion bulk flow vector $\mathbf{v}_i$ — the full [ion_velocity](name:ion_velocity) — projected onto the local magnetic field unit vector $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. It arises as the parallel projection of the first velocity-space moment of the ion distribution function, averaged over all charge states.

$$
v_{i,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_i \cdot \hat{b} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_i \cdot \mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ its magnitude.

In parallel momentum balance, $v_{i,\parallel}$ governs field-aligned particle transport through the divergence of the parallel particle flux $n_i v_{i,\parallel}$, where $n_i$ is the ion number density. In the scrape-off layer, $v_{i,\parallel}$ approaches the Bohm sound speed $c_s = \sqrt{(T_e + \gamma_i T_i)/m_i}$ at divertor targets, where $T_e$ and $T_i$ are the electron and ion temperatures and $m_i$ is the ion mass, imposing the sheath entrance boundary condition. It is inferred from spectroscopic Doppler-shift measurements, including charge exchange recombination spectroscopy. Typical values are near zero in the symmetric core and reach $10^4$–$10^5$ m/s in the scrape-off layer and divertor regions. For charge-state-resolved parallel flows see [parallel_ion_state_velocity](name:parallel_ion_state_velocity); the analogous electron quantity is [parallel_electron_velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity), and the cross-field component is [radial_ion_velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the ion flow is directed along the local magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_momentum_effective_convection_velocity
NAMES.short: Effective radial convection velocity multiplying the flux-surface-averaged ion momentum component parallel to the magnetic field in a transport model. It parameterizes pinch-like transport of that momentum component across flux surfaces, not ion motion along a field line.
NAMES.long:
Parallel momentum effective convection velocity is the scalar transport coefficient that multiplies the flux-surface-averaged ion momentum component parallel to the magnetic field in a radial transport model. It describes pinch-like transport of that signed momentum component across nested flux surfaces, and is distinct from the ion flow velocity along the magnetic field.

In a local diffusion-convection representation of radial parallel-momentum transport, the effective convection velocity is the coefficient $V_{M_{\parallel i}}$ in

$$
\Gamma_{M_{\parallel i}} = -D_{M_{\parallel i}} \frac{\partial M_{\parallel i}}{\partial r_\rho} + V_{M_{\parallel i}} M_{\parallel i}
$$

where $M_{\parallel i}$ is the flux-surface-averaged ion parallel momentum density in kg.m^-2.s^-1, $\Gamma_{M_{\parallel i}}$ is its radial flux across a flux surface in kg.m^-1.s^-2, $D_{M_{\parallel i}}$ is the effective diffusion coefficient in m^2.s^-1, $V_{M_{\parallel i}}$ is this effective convection velocity in m.s^-1, and $r_\rho$ is a distance-like radial flux-surface coordinate that increases outward from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary.

The coefficient is inferred from momentum-balance analysis, transport-model fitting, or predictive neoclassical and turbulent transport calculations. Experimental constraints commonly include ion rotation measurements, density and temperature, magnetic-equilibrium geometry, external torque estimates, and momentum source and sink terms; as an effective coefficient it can absorb unresolved pinch and off-diagonal transport effects.

Typical inferred core values in tokamaks are of order a few tens of m.s^-1 in magnitude, with larger effective values near strong rotation or pressure gradients and toward the edge transport region; the coefficient can change sign between inward and outward momentum convection.
NAMES.sign: Positive when, for positive ion parallel momentum density, the convective contribution to the radial momentum flux is directed toward increasing $r_\rho$, from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Signed component of the neutral energy flux in the direction of the local magnetic field. It represents the field-aligned projection of energy carried by neutral atoms or molecules in edge and scrape-off-layer transport.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral energy flux is the signed scalar projection of the neutral energy-flux vector onto the local magnetic-field direction. It measures the rate at which neutral-carried energy crosses a unit area whose normal is aligned with the magnetic field, after summing over the neutral populations represented in the physical model.

The projection is defined by

$$
q_{\parallel,n} = \mathbf{q}_n \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $q_{\parallel,n}$ is the parallel neutral energy flux in W m$^{-2}$, $\mathbf{q}_n$ is the total neutral energy-flux vector in W m$^{-2}$, $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector.

In transport calculations this quantity is obtained from kinetic, fluid, or Monte Carlo neutral descriptions by forming the neutral energy-flux vector from directed motion, thermal energy, and internal-state contributions, then projecting it onto $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ at the point of evaluation. It is especially useful in edge plasma and scrape-off-layer analysis, where recycling, ionization, molecular dissociation, and charge exchange couple neutral energy transport to the charged plasma.

Typical absolute magnitudes in tokamak edge and scrape-off-layer modeling are about $10^2$-$10^6$ W m$^{-2}$. Local values near intense divertor recycling, strong gas puffing, or energetic charge-exchange sources can approach $10^7$ W m$^{-2}$, while detached or weakly fueled regions may be much smaller.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral energy-flux vector has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Parallel neutral momentum flux is the neutral momentum-flux tensor projected twice along the local magnetic-field direction. It represents transport of parallel linear momentum through a surface normal to that direction, summed over neutral species and internal states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral momentum flux is the parallel-parallel component of the [neutral_momentum_flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) tensor. It describes transport of linear momentum whose component is along the local magnetic field through a surface whose normal is also along that field. The aggregate quantity sums over neutral species and internal states, whereas [parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux) resolves the same quantity for a single neutral state.

A kinetic definition is the second velocity moment of the neutral distribution along the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
\Pi_{n,\parallel} = \sum_a m_a \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{b})^2 f_a(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $a$ labels neutral species and internal states, $m_a$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, and $f_a$ is normalized so that $\int f_a\,d^3v=n_a$. In a fluid closure the contribution of state $a$ is commonly written inline as $m_a n_a u_{\parallel,a}^2 + P_{\parallel,a}$, where $u_{\parallel,a}$ is the mean parallel neutral velocity and $P_{\parallel,a}$ is the parallel component of the kinetic pressure tensor. Reversing the chosen direction of $\mathbf{b}$ does not change this double projection.

In practice this quantity is computed either directly from neutral kinetic distributions or from fluid moments such as density, mean parallel flow, and parallel pressure. Its divergence appears in the neutral parallel momentum balance and in momentum exchange with ions through charge-exchange, elastic scattering, ionization, and recombination terms. It is related to [parallel_neutral_particle_flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux), which is the signed first velocity moment of neutral number transport, to [toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux), and to [parallel_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity](name:parallel_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity).

Typical magnitudes are $10^{-4}-1$ kg m^-1 s^-2 for tenuous main-chamber or scrape-off-layer neutrals and $1-100$ kg m^-1 s^-2 in dense divertor or detached conditions. High-recycling transients or strong gas fueling can reach several $10^2$ kg m^-1 s^-2. Values depend most strongly on neutral density, atomic mass, directed parallel speed, and parallel neutral temperature.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Net number flux of neutral atoms and molecules per unit area along the local magnetic field direction, integrated over all neutral species and atomic or molecular states.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral particle flux is the component of the neutral particle flux density projected along the local magnetic field direction $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$. Defined as the species-integrated quantity over all neutral atoms and molecules and their internal states, it characterizes the dominant transport channel for neutrals along field lines in the edge and scrape-off-layer plasma. Together with [poloidal_neutral_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), it spans the principal directional decomposition of edge neutral transport.

The neutral continuity equation couples this flux to the local neutral number density $n_0$:

$$
\frac{\partial n_0}{\partial t} + \nabla_\parallel \Gamma_\parallel^{0} + \nabla_\perp \cdot \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_\perp^{0} = S_0
$$

where $\nabla_\parallel = \hat{b} \cdot \nabla$ is the derivative along the magnetic field line, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_\perp^{0}$ is the cross-field neutral flux, and $S_0$ is the net volumetric source rate accounting for ionization, recombination, and charge-exchange reactions.

This quantity is computed by edge plasma transport codes solving neutral fluid or kinetic equations in complex scrape-off-layer and divertor geometry. Results can be validated indirectly against neutral pressure gage measurements and visible spectroscopy of charge-exchange and recycling emission. The state-resolved energy counterpart [parallel_neutral_state_energy_flux](name:parallel_neutral_state_energy_flux) tracks energy transport per individual neutral state, while [parallel_ion_state_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_state_particle_flux) provides the analogous parallel ion particle channel.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral particles flow in the direction of the local magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_energy_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Component of the neutral-particle energy flux density, for a specified internal quantum state, projected along the local magnetic field direction.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral-state energy flux is the field-aligned component of the energy flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state. Although neutral particles are not magnetized, this projection is useful for comparing neutral energy transport with charged-particle transport along magnetic-field-aligned directions.

The parallel component is defined by projecting the neutral-state energy flux vector onto the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
q_{\parallel,s} = \mathbf{q}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $q_{\parallel,s}$ is the parallel energy flux density for neutral state $s$, $\mathbf{q}_s$ is the neutral-state energy flux vector with units W m$^{-2}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the dimensionless unit vector along the local magnetic field.

In edge and divertor plasma modeling, this quantity is computed from neutral kinetic, fluid, or collisional-radiative descriptions by combining the energy carried by neutrals in state $s$ with their velocity distribution and projecting the resulting energy flux onto $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$. It may include kinetic, internal excitation, ionization-potential, or model-defined state energy contributions depending on the energy convention used for $\mathbf{q}_s$.

Typical magnitudes in edge and divertor plasmas range from about 1-10^5 W m$^{-2}$ for weakly populated or localized neutral states, and can reach 10^5-10^7 W m$^{-2}$ in dense recycling regions or near strong neutral sources.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral-state energy flux vector has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field vector.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_momentum
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the momentum source acting on a specified neutral species state.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral state momentum is the component along the local magnetic field of the momentum source acting on one resolved neutral species state. It captures directed momentum exchange between neutrals and the plasma through elastic collisions, charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and related atomic processes.

The component is obtained by projecting the state-resolved neutral momentum-source vector onto the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
S_{\parallel,n} = \mathbf{S}_{p,n} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $S_{\parallel,n}$ is the parallel neutral state momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{p,n}$ is the momentum-source vector for neutral state $n$, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the magnetic field. The projection preserves the source unit kg m^-1 s^-2.

This quantity is usually computed rather than directly measured, using neutral transport or collisional-radiative modeling constrained by plasma density, temperature, flow, and neutral diagnostic information. Contributions from the relevant reaction channels are accumulated for the selected state and projected onto $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$; summing over neutral states gives the state-summed parallel neutral momentum source. Companion radial and toroidal components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, use projections along $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{\phi}$ instead of along the magnetic field.

Typical magnitudes in edge and scrape-off-layer transport calculations span 10^-6-10^2 kg m^-1 s^-2 for weakly interacting neutral populations and can reach 10^2-10^4 kg m^-1 s^-2 in dense divertor recycling or charge-exchange regions. Values vary strongly with neutral density, state population, ion temperature, flow speed, and reaction rates.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the projected momentum source is directed along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_momentum_convection_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Magnetic-field-parallel component of the effective convection velocity used for advective momentum transport of a specified neutral species state.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral-state momentum convection velocity is the component along the local magnetic field of an effective velocity coefficient that advects the momentum density associated with a specified neutral species state. It is a closure quantity for momentum transport and need not equal the bulk velocity of neutral particles.

In an effective-flux decomposition for the scalar parallel momentum density, it may be defined from the advective part of the momentum-density flux as:

$$
v_{\mathrm{mom},\parallel}^{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{adv}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{b}}}{M_\parallel}
$$

where $M_\parallel=m_n n_n u_{n,\parallel}$ is the neutral-state parallel momentum density, $m_n$ is the particle mass of the state, $n_n$ is its density, $u_{n,\parallel}$ is its bulk velocity component along the magnetic field, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{M_\parallel}^{\mathrm{adv}}$ is the advective flux of that momentum density, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}=\boldsymbol{B}/|\boldsymbol{B}|$ is the magnetic-field unit vector. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, $\boldsymbol{B}=B_R\hat{R}+B_\phi\hat{\phi}+B_Z\hat{Z}$; the parallel projection is along $\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}$ rather than along any single coordinate direction. When $M_\parallel$ is zero, the coefficient is defined by the transport closure rather than by the ratio alone.

The coefficient is usually obtained from a fluid closure or from moments of a kinetic neutral calculation after separating advective transport from diffusion, viscosity, and local source or sink terms. Because ionization, recombination, recycling, and charge-exchange processes can be folded into an effective closure, this velocity can differ from the actual neutral flow velocity.

Typical absolute magnitudes are 1-10^4 m.s^-1 in edge neutral-fluid calculations, with values near zero at stagnation surfaces. Fast charge-exchange or recycling populations can give effective values of 10^4-10^5 m.s^-1, and the sign may change along a field line or across regions with opposing neutral momentum flow.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the effective momentum-convection velocity points along the magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\boldsymbol{b}}=\boldsymbol{B}/|\boldsymbol{B}|$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_momentum_diffusivity
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Diffusion coefficient governing field-line-parallel transport of momentum for neutral particles in a specific neutral species state.
NAMES.long:
The parallel momentum diffusivity for a neutral state is the field-aligned component of the momentum diffusion coefficient for neutral particles resolved into a specific internal or quantum state. It enters the parallel momentum transport equation as the proportionality between the diffusive momentum flux and the gradient of the parallel flow velocity along the magnetic field, closing the neutral fluid momentum balance in the field-aligned direction.

The parallel diffusive momentum flux for the neutral state is:

$$
\Gamma_{m,\parallel} = -m_n \, n_n \, D_{\parallel} \, \nabla_{\!\parallel} v_{\parallel}
$$

where $m_n$ is the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ is the neutral state number density, $v_{\parallel}$ is the parallel flow velocity, and $\nabla_{\!\parallel} = \hat{b} \cdot \nabla$ is the gradient along the unit magnetic field direction $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/B$.

This quantity is the momentum-transport counterpart to [parallel_neutral_state_diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_state_diffusivity), which governs particle number density transport rather than momentum. The analogous coefficient for ion charge states is [parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), while parallel_momentum_diffusivity represents the total edge-plasma momentum diffusivity without state resolution. Values are supplied by transport closure schemes derived from kinetic theory or fluid approximations, and reflect the collisional and streaming processes redistributing neutral momentum along field lines in the edge and divertor regions.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Field-parallel component of the neutral-state momentum flux density for a specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It represents transport of neutral-particle momentum along the local magnetic-field direction per unit area and time.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral-state momentum flux is the field-aligned scalar component of the second-rank momentum-flux tensor for neutrals in a specified state. The state qualifier identifies the atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state whose neutral population is being followed; summing over states gives the corresponding state-integrated neutral momentum flux. The field-aligned direction is defined by the unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ along the local magnetic field.

For a momentum-flux tensor $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ of neutral state $s$, the parallel component is defined by contracting the tensor with the field-aligned direction on both indices:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}^{(s)} = \hat{\mathbf{b}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ gives the flux of vector momentum per unit area and time, and $\Pi_{\parallel}^{(s)}$ is the flux of field-aligned momentum through a surface whose positive normal is field-aligned. In an isotropic fluid closure this reduces locally to the advective-plus-pressure contribution $m_s n_s u_{\parallel}^2 + p_s$, with $m_s$ the neutral particle mass, $n_s$ the state-resolved density, $u_{\parallel}$ the bulk velocity along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, and $p_s$ the scalar pressure; kinetic or anisotropic closures replace $p_s$ by the appropriate parallel pressure contribution.

This quantity is computed from state-resolved neutral distribution moments in fluid, kinetic, or Monte Carlo neutral-transport calculations. It is usually constrained indirectly by diagnostics sensitive to neutral density, temperature, flow, recycling, and charge-exchange source terms rather than measured as a direct local tensor component. Related geometric components, such as toroidal or vertical momentum flux, are defined relative to the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Typical magnitudes are strongly regime dependent because neutral density and velocity vary by many orders of magnitude between the confined plasma, scrape-off layer, divertor, and recycling region. Order-of-magnitude values may range from about $10^{-8}$-$10^{-2}$ kg m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$ for dilute energetic neutral populations to $10^{-3}$-$10$ kg m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$ in dense edge or divertor neutral regions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when positive field-aligned neutral momentum is transported through a surface whose positive normal is in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_particle_flux
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the particle flux for neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal state, resolved along the magnetic field direction in the edge plasma.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral-state particle flux quantifies the number of neutral atoms or molecules occupying a specified internal quantum state (electronic, vibrational, or rotational) that cross a unit area per unit time along the direction parallel to the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. Resolving the flux by internal state is essential in edge plasma models because reaction rates for ionization, charge exchange, and dissociation depend critically on which state the neutral population occupies.

The flux is defined as:

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,s} = n_s \, v_{\parallel,s}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of neutrals in internal state $s$ and $v_{\parallel,s}$ is their mean velocity component parallel to $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity is distinct from [parallel_neutral_particle_flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux), which integrates over all internal states. The complementary poloidal projection is [poloidal_neutral_state_particle_flux](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_flux), and the energy transport carried by the same state-resolved neutral population is described by [parallel_neutral_state_energy_flux](name:parallel_neutral_state_energy_flux). The ion analog, resolved by charge state, is [parallel_ion_state_particle_flux](name:parallel_ion_state_particle_flux). In the edge and divertor regions, typical magnitudes range from $10^{19}$ to $10^{22}$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, with peak values occurring near the divertor target plates where neutral recycling is strongest.
NAMES.sign: Positive when neutral particles in the specified state flow in the direction of the local magnetic field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
NAMES.subject: neutral_state
NAMES.short: Parallel component of the electric-field cross magnetic-field drift velocity assigned to a neutral species state, taken along the local magnetic-field direction. For a pure E cross B drift this projection vanishes because the drift is perpendicular to the magnetic field; nonzero values indicate model or numerical residuals rather than a physical parallel drift.
NAMES.long:
The parallel neutral-state velocity due to the $E\times B$ drift is the scalar component, along the local magnetic-field direction, of the velocity contribution labeled as $E\times B$ drift for a selected neutral species state. The drift itself is species independent; the neutral-state label identifies the population to which this velocity contribution is assigned. A pure $E\times B$ drift is exactly perpendicular to the magnetic field, so its physical parallel projection vanishes.

For neutral-state label $n$, the defining projection is

$$
v_{\parallel,E\times B}^{(n)} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}^{(n)} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{B^2} = 0
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field in V.m^-1, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field in T, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B$ is the dimensionless unit vector along the magnetic field, and the superscript $n$ labels the neutral species state rather than a power. The scalar $v_{\parallel,E\times B}^{(n)}$ has unit m.s^-1. The final equality follows from the vector identity $\mathbf{B}\cdot(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})=0$.

The quantity is normally computed from electric-field or electrostatic-potential estimates together with the local magnetic field, followed by projection along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$. Nonzero values for this pure contribution are interpreted as numerical residuals, field-projection inconsistencies, or an explicitly documented model-decomposition convention, not as a physical drift along the magnetic field caused by magnetic geometry.

The expected physical value is 0 m.s^-1. In practical calculations, any nonzero residual should be small compared with the related [radial](name:radial_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), [poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), and [toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) components of [neutral-state velocity due to E cross B drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift); no universal residual range is meaningful because it depends on the numerical and modeling procedure. The analogous ion quantity is [parallel ion-state velocity due to E cross B drift](name:parallel_ion_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).
NAMES.sign: Positive when the component is directed along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

NAMES.name: parallel_neutral_velocity
NAMES.subject: neutral
NAMES.short: Neutral particle bulk flow velocity projected along the local magnetic field direction, averaged over all internal quantum states of the neutral species. It is a signed parallel velocity, positive for flow along the magnetic field.
NAMES.long:
Parallel neutral velocity is the component of the neutral species bulk flow parallel to the local magnetic field direction. It describes directed motion of neutral atoms or molecules along field-aligned transport paths after averaging over all internal quantum states of the species.

The signed parallel component is defined by projecting the neutral bulk velocity onto the magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
v_{\parallel,n} = \mathbf{v}_n \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_n$ is the state-averaged neutral bulk velocity and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. When state-resolved neutral velocities are available, $\mathbf{v}_n$ is typically the density-weighted average over internal states.

This quantity is inferred from neutral transport modeling, kinetic or fluid simulations, and spectroscopic measurements sensitive to Doppler shifts of neutral emission. It is useful for separating field-aligned neutral transport from cross-field or poloidal components, especially in edge, scrape-off-layer, and divertor plasmas.

Typical magnitudes in magnetically confined fusion plasmas range from $10^3-10^5$ m.s^-1, depending on neutral temperature, source localization, charge-exchange coupling, and divertor or edge plasma conditions.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the neutral bulk flow has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

NAMES.name: parallel_non_inductive_current_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density driven by all non-inductive mechanisms, encompassing bootstrap current and externally driven contributions from RF wave heating and neutral beam injection.
NAMES.long:
The parallel non-inductive current density represents all plasma current flowing parallel to the magnetic field that is sustained by mechanisms other than the inductive electric field. It encompasses neoclassical bootstrap current and externally driven contributions including neutral beam injection, electron cyclotron current drive, lower hybrid current drive, and ion cyclotron current drive.

The quantity is defined as the flux-surface average of the non-inductive current density projected onto the magnetic field, normalized to a reference on-axis field $B_0$:

$$
j_{ni,\parallel} = \frac{\langle \mathbf{j}_{ni} \cdot \mathbf{B} \rangle}{B_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{ni}$ is the non-inductive current density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, $\langle \cdots \rangle$ denotes the flux-surface average, and $B_0$ is the reference toroidal field at the magnetic axis.

This profile is computed by summing independently modeled contributions: the [bootstrap current density] from pressure-gradient-driven neoclassical transport, and the externally driven component from wave or particle injection schemes. Together with [ohmic current density](name:parallel_ohmic_current_density), which captures the inductively driven resistive channel, the sum yields the [total parallel current density](name:parallel_current_density).

In high-performance H-mode plasmas the non-inductive fraction ranges from 5–30% in conventional scenarios to near unity in fully non-inductive advanced tokamak operation. Peak magnitudes span $10^5$–$10^7$ A m$^{-2}$ across medium-to-large devices.
NAMES.sign: Positive when the non-inductive current is directed along the magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$, i.e., when $\langle \mathbf{j}_{ni} \cdot \mathbf{B} \rangle > 0$.

NAMES.name: parallel_ohmic_current_density
NAMES.short: Flux-surface-averaged parallel current density driven inductively by the parallel electric field, representing the resistively sustained component of the total plasma current.
NAMES.long:
The ohmic parallel current density is the inductively driven component of the total parallel plasma current, sustained by the parallel electric field through resistive processes described by Ohm's law.
